sentences.zh: 岷莊王楩，太祖第十八子。洪武二十四年封國岷州。二十八年以雲南新附，宜親王鎮撫，改雲南。有司請營宮殿，帝令斬居棕亭，俟民力稍紓後作。建文元年，西平侯沐晟奏其過，廢為庶人，徙漳州。永樂初復王，與晟交惡。帝賜書諭楩，而詔戒晟。楩沈湎廢禮，擅收諸司印信，殺戮吏民。帝怒，奪冊寶。尋念王建文中久幽系，復予之，而楩不悛。六年，削其護衛，罷官屬。仁宗即位，徙武岡，寄居州治。久之，始建王邸。景泰元年薨。子恭王徽煣嗣。

translations.literal: Zhu Pian, Prince Zhuang of Min, was the Founding Emperor's eighteenth son. In Hongwu year twenty-four he was enfeoffed with his state at Minzhou. In year twenty-eight, because Yunnan had newly submitted and it was fitting that a prince of the blood should pacify and govern it, his fief was changed to Yunnan. The responsible officials requested that palaces be built, but the emperor ordered him for the moment to live in a palm pavilion and wait until the people's strength had somewhat recovered before building. In Jianwen year one, Mu Sheng, Marquis of Xiping, memorialized his faults; he was reduced to commoner status and moved to Zhangzhou. At the beginning of Yongle his princely title was restored, but he was on bad terms with Sheng. The emperor bestowed a letter admonishing Pian and issued an edict warning Sheng. Pian sank into drink, abandoned ritual, arbitrarily seized the seals of the offices, and killed officials and commoners. The emperor was angry and took away his patent and seal. Soon, remembering that the prince had long been imprisoned during Jianwen, he restored them to him, but Pian did not reform. In year six his guards were cut down and his officials dismissed. When Renzong came to the throne, Pian was moved to Wugang and lodged in the prefectural seat. After a long time, a princely residence was finally built. He died in Jingtai year one. His son Zhu Huirou, Prince Gong, succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Pian, Prince Zhuang of Min, was the founding emperor's eighteenth son. In Hongwu 24 he was enfeoffed at Minzhou. In Hongwu 28, because Yunnan had only recently submitted and needed a prince of the blood to pacify it, his fief was changed to Yunnan. When officials proposed building a palace, the emperor ordered him to live for the time being in a palm pavilion and wait until the people had somewhat recovered before construction began. In Jianwen 1, Mu Sheng, Marquis of Xiping, memorialized his offenses, and Pian was reduced to commoner status and moved to Zhangzhou. Early in Yongle his title was restored, but he quarreled with Mu Sheng. The emperor sent Pian an admonitory letter and issued an edict warning Mu Sheng. Pian then sank into drunkenness, abandoned ritual, seized official seals on his own authority, and killed officials and commoners. Angered, the emperor stripped him of his patent and seal. Before long, remembering that Pian had been imprisoned for years under Jianwen, the emperor restored them, but Pian did not reform. In Yongle 6 his guards were reduced and his officials dismissed. When Renzong came to the throne, Pian was moved to Wugang and lodged in the prefectural offices. Only after some time was a princely residence built. He died in Jingtai 1, and his son Zhu Huirou, Prince Gong, succeeded.

sentences.zh: 初，世子徽焲，宣德初，訐其弟鎮南王徽煣誹謗仁廟。

translations.literal: Initially, the heir apparent Huiji, in the early Xuande reign, accused his younger brother the Prince of Zhennan Huiyu of slandering the Ren Temple.
translations.idiomatic: At first the heir apparent Huiji, early in the Xuande reign, denounced his younger brother the Prince of Zhennan, Huiyu, for slandering the late Ren Emperor.

sentences.zh: 宣宗疑其詐，並召至京，及所連閹豎面質，事果誣，斬閹豎而遣徽煣等歸。

translations.literal: The Xuande Emperor suspected fraud, summoned both to the capital, and confronted the implicated eunuchs in person; the matter proved false, the eunuchs were executed, and Huiyu and the others were sent back.
translations.idiomatic: The Xuande Emperor suspected a frame-up, summoned both brothers to the capital, and confronted the eunuchs implicated in the case face to face. The charge proved false; the eunuchs were executed and Huiyu and the others were sent home.

sentences.zh: 徽煣嗣位。

translations.literal: Huiyu succeeded to the title.
translations.idiomatic: Huiyu then succeeded to the princedom.

sentences.zh: 弟廣通王徽煠有勇力，家人段友洪以技術得寵。

translations.literal: His younger brother the Prince of Guangtong Huiye was brave and strong; the household retainer Duan Youhong won favor through technical arts.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother the Prince of Guangtong, Huiye, was strong and martial; a household retainer named Duan Youhong won favor through occult arts.

sentences.zh: 致仕後軍都事於利賓言徽煠有異相，當主天下，遂謀亂。

translations.literal: The retired Rear Army commandant Yu Libin said Huiye had an extraordinary physiognomy and ought to rule the realm, whereupon they plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Libin, a retired commandant of the Rear Army, declared that Huiye bore an extraordinary countenance and was destined to rule the realm, and they thereupon plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 作偽敕，分遣友洪及蒙能、陳添行入苗中，誘諸苗以銀印金幣，使發兵攻武岡。

translations.literal: They forged an imperial edict and separately sent Youhong, Meng Neng, and Chen Tianxing among the Miao, tempting the various Miao with silver seals and gold coins to raise troops and attack Wugang.
translations.idiomatic: They forged an imperial edict and dispatched Youhong, Meng Neng, and Chen Tianxing into Miao territory, tempting the chiefs with silver seals and gold coins to raise troops and attack Wugang.

sentences.zh: 苗首楊文伯等不敢受。

translations.literal: The Miao leaders Yang Wenbo and others dared not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The Miao chiefs Yang Wenbo and others dared not accept.

sentences.zh: 事覺，友洪為徽煣所執。

translations.literal: When the plot was exposed, Youhong was seized by Huiyu.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot came to light, Youhong was seized by Huiyu.

sentences.zh: 都御史李實以聞，遣駙馬都尉焦敬、中官李琮徵徽煠入京師。

translations.literal: The censor-in-chief Li Shi reported it; the emperor sent the commandant-escort Jiao Jing and the eunuch Li Cong to summon Huiye to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Li Shi reported the matter, and the court sent Commandant-escort Jiao Jing and the eunuch Li Cong to summon Huiye to the capital.

sentences.zh: 湖廣總管王來、總兵官梁缶復發陽宗王徽焟通謀狀，亦徵入。

translations.literal: The Huguang grand coordinator Wang Lai and the regional commander Liang Fou again exposed the Prince of Yangzong Huiyun's complicity, and he too was summoned.
translations.idiomatic: Grand coordinator Wang Lai of Huguang and regional commander Liang Fou also exposed the Prince of Yangzong, Huiyun, as a co-conspirator, and he too was summoned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 皆除爵，幽高墻。

translations.literal: All were stripped of rank and confined within high walls.
translations.idiomatic: All were stripped of their titles and immured in the inner palace compound.

sentences.zh: 時景泰二年十月也。

translations.literal: This was in the tenth month of the second year of the Jingtai reign.
translations.idiomatic: This was in the tenth month of the second year of the Jingtai reign.

sentences.zh: 天順七年，徽煣薨。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Tianshun, Huiyu died.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of the Tianshun reign, Huiyu died.

sentences.zh: 子順王音嗣，病瘋痹，屢年不起。

translations.literal: His son the Prince of Shun Yin succeeded; he suffered from paralysis and for years could not rise.
translations.idiomatic: His son the Prince of Shun, Yin, succeeded him but was stricken with paralysis and for years could not leave his bed.

sentences.zh: 次子安昌王膺鋪侍醫藥，晨夕不去左右。

translations.literal: The second son the Prince of Anchang Yingpu attended him with medicine, morning and evening never leaving his side.
translations.idiomatic: His second son the Prince of Anchang, Yingpu, tended him with medicines and never left his side from morning till night.

sentences.zh: 憲宗聞之，賜敕嘉獎。

translations.literal: When the Xianzong Emperor heard of it, he bestowed an edict of praise.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xianzong Emperor heard of this, he issued an edict commending him.

sentences.zh: 成化十六年，音薨。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Chenghua, Yin died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year of the Chenghua reign, Yin died.

sentences.zh: 世子膺鉟居喪，飲博無度，承奉劉忠禁制之，遂殺忠。

translations.literal: The heir apparent Yingbo during mourning drank and gambled without restraint; the attendant Liu Zhong restrained him, whereupon he killed Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: During the mourning period the heir apparent Yingbo drank and gambled without restraint. His attendant Liu Zhong tried to restrain him, and Yingbo killed him.

sentences.zh: 事聞，驗實，革冠帶停封。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported and verified, his cap and belt were removed and his succession suspended.
translations.idiomatic: When the matter was reported and verified, he was stripped of his cap and belt and his succession was suspended.

sentences.zh: 居四年，乃嗣。

translations.literal: After four years he was allowed to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: After four years he was permitted to succeed.

sentences.zh: 弘治十三年薨，謚曰簡。

translations.literal: He died in the thirteenth year of Hongzhi; his posthumous title was Jian.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the thirteenth year of the Hongzhi reign and was given the posthumous title Jian (Plain).

sentences.zh: 子靖王彥汰嗣。

translations.literal: His son the Prince of Jing Yantai succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son the Prince of Jing, Yantai, succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖四年，與弟南安王彥泥訐陰事，彥泥廢為庶人，彥汰亦坐抗制擅權革爵。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiajing, he and his younger brother the Prince of Nan'an Yan'ni denounced each other's secret affairs; Yan'ni was degraded to commoner status, and Yantai also lost his title for resisting orders and usurping authority.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the Jiajing reign he and his younger brother the Prince of Nan'an, Yan'ni, denounced each other's secret wrongdoing. Yan'ni was reduced to commoner status, and Yantai also lost his title for defying the court and arrogating power.

sentences.zh: 八年令世子譽榮攝府事。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the heir apparent Yurong was ordered to administer the fief.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year the heir apparent Yurong was ordered to administer the princedom.

sentences.zh: 譽榮上疏懇辭，謂：「臣坐享尊榮，而父困苦寂寞，臣心何安！

translations.literal: Yurong submitted a memorial earnestly declining, saying: "Your subject sits enjoying honor and glory while his father suffers hardship and loneliness—how can his heart be at ease!
translations.idiomatic: Yurong submitted a memorial earnestly declining, saying, "Your subject enjoys rank and honor while his father lives in hardship and loneliness—how can my heart be at ease!

sentences.zh: 且前曾舉臣弟善化王譽桔，廷議以子無制父理，奏寢不行。

translations.literal: Moreover, I previously recommended my younger brother the Prince of Shanhua Yujie; the court debated that a son ought not rule over his father, and the memorial was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, I once recommended my younger brother the Prince of Shanhua, Yujie, but the court held that a son must not govern his father, and the proposal was set aside.

sentences.zh: 臣亦人子也，獨不愧臣弟乎！」

translations.literal: Your subject is also a son—should he alone not feel ashamed before his younger brother!"
translations.idiomatic: I too am a son—should I not feel ashamed before my younger brother!"

sentences.zh: 帝覽疏憐之，下部議。

translations.literal: The emperor read the memorial with compassion and referred it to the ministries for discussion.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the memorial with compassion and referred the matter to the ministries for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 十二年賜彥汰冠帶，理府事。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year Yantai was granted cap and belt and allowed to administer the fief.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year Yantai was restored to cap and belt and permitted to administer the princedom.

sentences.zh: 十五年，以兩宮徽號恩復王。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, by grace of the honorific titles for the two palaces, he was restored as prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year, by grace of the honorific titles granted to the two palaces, his princely title was restored.

sentences.zh: 又八年始薨。

translations.literal: Eight years later he died.
translations.idiomatic: Eight years later he died.

sentences.zh: 子康王譽榮嗣，三十一年薨。

translations.literal: His son the Prince of Kang Yurong succeeded and died in the thirty-first year.
translations.idiomatic: His son the Prince of Kang, Yurong, succeeded him and died in the thirty-first year of his reign.

sentences.zh: 子憲王定耀嗣，三十四年薨。

translations.literal: His son the Prince of Xian Dingyao succeeded and died in the thirty-fourth year.
translations.idiomatic: His son the Prince of Xian, Dingyao, succeeded and died in the thirty-fourth year.

sentences.zh: 曾孫禋洪，天啟二年嗣，崇禎元年薨。

translations.literal: The great-grandson Yin Hong succeeded in the second year of Tianqi and died in the first year of Chongzhen.
translations.idiomatic: The great-grandson Yin Hong succeeded in the second year of the Tianqi reign and died in the first year of the Chongzhen reign.

sentences.zh: 無子，從父企嗣。

translations.literal: Having no son, his collateral relative Qi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: He had no son, and a collateral relative named Qi succeeded.

sentences.zh: 十六年，流賊陷武岡遇害。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, when roving bandits took Wugang, he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year, when roving rebels seized Wugang, he was killed.

sentences.zh: 谷王橞，太祖第十九子。

translations.literal: Prince of Gu Yi was the Taizu Emperor's nineteenth son.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Gu, Yi, was the nineteenth son of the Taizu Emperor.

sentences.zh: 洪武二十四年封。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed in the twenty-fourth year of Hongwu.
translations.idiomatic: He received his enfeoffment in the twenty-fourth year of the Hongwu reign.

sentences.zh: 二十八年三月就藩宣府。

translations.literal: In the third month of the twenty-eighth year he went to his fief at Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the twenty-eighth year he went to take up his fief at Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 宣府，上谷地，故曰谷王。

translations.literal: Xuanfu was in the Shanggu region, hence the title Prince of Gu.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanfu lay in the Shanggu region, hence the title Prince of Gu (Valley).

sentences.zh: 燕兵起，橞走還京師。

translations.literal: When the Yan army rose, Yi fled back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yan armies rose, Yi fled back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 及燕師渡江，橞奉命守金川門，登城望見成祖麾蓋，開門迎降。

translations.literal: When the Yan forces crossed the Yangzi, Yi was ordered to hold the Jinchuan Gate; he mounted the wall, saw Chengzu's banner, and opened the gate to welcome surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yan forces crossed the Yangzi, Yi was ordered to hold the Jinchuan Gate. He mounted the wall, saw Chengzu's banner and canopy, and opened the gate to welcome them in.

sentences.zh: 成祖德之，即位，賜橞樂七奏，衛士三百，賚予甚厚。

translations.literal: Chengzu was grateful; upon his accession he granted Yi seven musical pieces, three hundred guards, and very generous gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzu was deeply grateful. Upon his accession he granted Yi a seven-piece musical establishment, three hundred guards, and exceedingly generous rewards.

sentences.zh: 改封長沙，增歲祿二千石。

translations.literal: He was reassigned to Changsha and his annual stipend increased by two thousand piculs.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned to Changsha and his annual stipend was increased by two thousand piculs.

sentences.zh: 橞居國橫甚，忠誠伯茹常過長沙不謁橞，橞白之帝，常得罪死。

translations.literal: Yi was extremely overbearing in his state; the Marquis of Zhongcheng Ru Chang passed through Changsha without calling on Yi, and Yi reported him to the emperor; Chang was condemned and died.
translations.idiomatic: Yi ruled his domain with extreme arrogance. When the Marquis of Zhongcheng, Ru Chang, passed through Changsha without paying a courtesy call, Yi reported him to the emperor, and Chang was condemned to death.

sentences.zh: 遂益驕肆，奪民田，侵公稅，殺無罪人。

translations.literal: He grew still more arrogant, seized commoners' fields, encroached on public taxes, and killed the innocent.
translations.idiomatic: He grew still more arrogant, seized commoners' land, diverted public revenues, and killed the innocent.

sentences.zh: 長史虞廷綱數諫，誣廷綱誹謗，磔殺之。

translations.literal: The chief administrator Yu Tinggang repeatedly remonstrated; he falsely accused Tinggang of slander and had him dismembered.
translations.idiomatic: Chief administrator Yu Tinggang remonstrated with him repeatedly. Yi falsely accused Tinggang of slander and had him executed by dismemberment.

sentences.zh: 招匿亡命，習兵法戰陣，造戰艦弓弩器械。

translations.literal: He recruited fugitives, drilled in military tactics and battle formations, and built warships, crossbows, and weapons.
translations.idiomatic: He harbored fugitives, drilled his men in tactics and battle formations, and built warships, crossbows, and other weapons.

sentences.zh: 大創佛寺，度僧千人，為咒詛。

translations.literal: He greatly expanded Buddhist temples, ordained a thousand monks, and used them for curses.
translations.idiomatic: He greatly expanded Buddhist temples, ordained a thousand monks, and employed them in curses and imprecations.

sentences.zh: 日與都指揮張成，宦者吳智、劉信謀，呼成「師尚父」，智、信「國老令公」。

translations.literal: Daily he plotted with the regional commander Zhang Cheng and the eunuchs Wu Zhi and Liu Xin, calling Cheng "Grand Tutor" and Zhi and Xin "Elder Statesmen of the Realm."
translations.idiomatic: Day after day he plotted with regional commander Zhang Cheng and the eunuchs Wu Zhi and Liu Xin, addressing Cheng as "Grand Tutor" and Zhi and Xin as "Elder Statesmen of the Realm."

sentences.zh: 偽引讖書，云：「我高皇帝十八子，與讖合。」

translations.literal: He falsely cited a prophecy book, saying: "Our August Emperor had eighteen sons—this accords with the prophecy."
translations.idiomatic: He falsely cited a prophecy, saying, "Our August Emperor had eighteen sons—this accords with the prophecy."

sentences.zh: 橞行次十九，以趙王杞早卒，故云。

translations.literal: Yi ranked nineteenth; because Prince of Zhao Qi died young, he said this.
translations.idiomatic: Yi ranked nineteenth; because the Prince of Zhao, Qi, had died young, he made this claim.

sentences.zh: 謀於元夕獻燈，選壯士教之音樂，同入禁中，伺隙為變。

translations.literal: He planned on the Lantern Festival to present lanterns, select strong men trained in music, enter the forbidden precinct together, and seize an opportunity for revolt.
translations.idiomatic: He planned to present lanterns on the Lantern Festival, select strong men trained in music, enter the inner palace with them, and seize an opportunity to stage a coup.

sentences.zh: 又致書蜀王為隱語，欲結蜀為援。

translations.literal: He also wrote to the Prince of Shu in cryptic language, wishing to win Shu as an ally.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote to the Prince of Shu in cryptic language, hoping to win Shu as an ally.

sentences.zh: 蜀王貽書切責。

translations.literal: The Prince of Shu sent a letter sharply rebuking him.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Shu sent back a letter sharply rebuking him.

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: He would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Yi would not listen.

sentences.zh: 己而蜀王子崇寧王悅燇得罪，逃橞所。

translations.literal: Soon the Prince of Shu's son the Prince of Chongning Yueyan offended and fled to Yi's residence.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Prince of Shu's son the Prince of Chongning, Yueyan, fell afoul of the law and fled to Yi's residence.

sentences.zh: 橞因詭眾：「往年我開金川門出建文君，今在邸中。

translations.literal: Yi thereupon deceived the crowd: "Years ago I opened the Jinchuan Gate and let out the Jianwen Emperor; he is now in my residence.
translations.idiomatic: Yi thereupon deceived his followers, saying, "Years ago I opened the Jinchuan Gate and let the Jianwen Emperor escape; he is now in my residence.

sentences.zh: 我將為申大義，事發有日矣。」

translations.literal: I shall uphold the great cause; the affair will break forth before long."
translations.idiomatic: I shall soon uphold the righteous cause; the day of action draws near."

sentences.zh: 蜀王聞之，上變告。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Shu heard of it, he reported the treason.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Shu heard of this, he reported the plot to the throne.

sentences.zh: 初，護衛都督僉事張興見橞為不法，懼禍及，因奏事北京，白其狀。

translations.literal: Earlier, the guard commandant Zhang Xing, seeing Yi's lawlessness, feared being implicated and, while reporting on business in Beijing, disclosed his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, guard commandant Zhang Xing, seeing Yi's lawlessness, feared being implicated and, while on business in Beijing, disclosed his conduct to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝不信。

translations.literal: The emperor did not believe it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not believe him.

sentences.zh: 興過南京，復啟於太子，且曰：「乞他日無連坐。」

translations.literal: Xing passed through Nanjing and again informed the crown prince, saying: "I beg that on another day there be no guilt by association."
translations.idiomatic: Passing through Nanjing, Xing informed the crown prince as well, saying, "I beg that when the day comes I not be punished by association."

sentences.zh: 至是，帝嘆曰：「朕待橞厚，張興常為朕言，不忍信，今果然。」

translations.literal: Now the emperor sighed: "I treated Yi generously; Zhang Xing often spoke to me, yet I could not bear to believe—now it has indeed come to pass."
translations.idiomatic: Now the emperor sighed and said, "I treated Yi generously. Zhang Xing often warned me, yet I could not bear to believe him—and now it has indeed come to pass."

sentences.zh: 立命中官持敕諭橞歸悅燇於蜀，且召橞入朝。

translations.literal: He immediately ordered a eunuch to carry an edict telling Yi to return Yueyan to Shu and summoning Yi to court.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately ordered a eunuch to carry an edict instructing Yi to return Yueyan to Shu and summoning Yi to court.

sentences.zh: 橞至，帝示以蜀王章，伏地請死。

translations.literal: When Yi arrived, the emperor showed him the Prince of Shu's memorial; he prostrated himself and begged for death.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi arrived, the emperor showed him the Prince of Shu's memorial. Yi prostrated himself and begged for death.

sentences.zh: 諸大臣廷劾橞曰：「周戮管、蔡，漢辟濞、長，皆大義滅親，陛下縱念橞，奈天下何？」

translations.literal: The ministers impeached Yi in court, saying: "Zhou executed Guan and Cai; Han punished Pi and Chang—all upheld righteousness over kinship. Even if Your Majesty pities Yi, what of the realm?"
translations.idiomatic: The ministers impeached Yi at court, saying, "Zhou executed Guan and Cai; Han punished Liu Pi and Liu Chang—all placed righteousness above kinship. Even if Your Majesty pities Yi, what of the realm?"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「橞，朕弟，朕且令諸兄弟議。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Yi is my younger brother; I shall have my brothers deliberate."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Yi is my younger brother. I shall have my brothers deliberate."

sentences.zh: 永樂十五年正月，周王橚、楚王楨、蜀王椿等各上議：「橞違祖訓，謀不軌，蹤跡甚著，大逆不道，誅無赦。」

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifteenth year of Yongle, the Princes of Zhou Su, Chu Zhen, and Shu Chun each submitted opinions: "Yi violated ancestral teachings, plotted rebellion, his traces are very clear—great treason, execution without pardon."
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifteenth year of Yongle, the Princes of Zhou, Chu, and Shu each submitted opinions: "Yi has violated ancestral teachings and plotted rebellion; the evidence is clear. This is great treason and he should be executed without pardon."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「諸王群臣奉大義，國法固爾，吾寧生橞？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The princes and ministers uphold righteousness; the law of the state is thus—how could I let Yi live?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The princes and ministers uphold righteousness, and the law of the state demands it—how could I let Yi live?"

sentences.zh: 於是及二子皆廢為庶人，官屬多誅死，興以先發不坐。

translations.literal: Thereupon he and his two sons were all degraded to commoners; many officials were executed; Xing was not punished for having reported first.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he and his two sons were all reduced to commoner status; many of his officials were executed; Xing was not punished because he had reported first.

sentences.zh: 韓憲王松，太祖第二十子。

translations.literal: Prince of Han, posthumous Xian, Song, was the Taizu Emperor's twentieth son.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Han, posthumously titled Xian, Song, was the twentieth son of the Taizu Emperor.

sentences.zh: 洪武二十四年封國開原。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Hongwu he was enfeoffed at Kaiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year of the Hongwu reign he was enfeoffed at Kaiyuan.

sentences.zh: 性英敏，通古今，恭謹無過。

translations.literal: By nature intelligent and keen, versed in past and present, respectful and cautious without fault.
translations.idiomatic: He was intelligent and keen by nature, versed in past and present learning, and respectful and cautious without fault.

sentences.zh: 永樂五年薨。

translations.literal: He died in the fifth year of Yongle.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth year of the Yongle reign.

sentences.zh: 以未之國，命葬安德門外。

translations.literal: Because he had not gone to his state, he was ordered buried outside Ande Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Because he had never gone to his fief, he was ordered buried outside Ande Gate.

sentences.zh: 十年，子恭王沖或嗣。

translations.literal: In the tenth year his son the Prince of Gong Chongran succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year his son the Prince of Gong, Chongran, succeeded.

sentences.zh: 時棄大寧三衛地，開原逼塞不可居。

translations.literal: At that time the three guards of Daning had been abandoned; Kaiyuan pressed the frontier and could not be inhabited.
translations.idiomatic: By then the three guards of Daning had been abandoned; Kaiyuan lay hard against the frontier and could not be inhabited.

sentences.zh: 二十二年改封平涼。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was reassigned to Pingliang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year the fief was moved to Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，召沖或與弟襄陵王沖秌、樂平王沖烌入朝，各獻詩頌。

translations.literal: When the Renzong Emperor acceded, he summoned Chongran with his younger brothers the Princes of Xiangling Chongqiu and Leping Chongxiu to court; each presented poems of praise.
translations.idiomatic: When the Renzong Emperor acceded, he summoned Chongran and his younger brothers the Princes of Xiangling, Chongqiu, and Leping, Chongxiu, to court, and each presented poems of praise.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉悅，賜金幣有差。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and granted gold and coins in varying amounts.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and granted gold and coins in varying amounts.

sentences.zh: 宣宗初，請徙江南。

translations.literal: Early in the Xuande reign he requested relocation to Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xuande reign he requested relocation to the south.

sentences.zh: 不許。

translations.literal: It was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was denied.

sentences.zh: 請蠲護衛屯租，建邸第。

translations.literal: He requested exemption of guard colony rents and construction of a residence.
translations.idiomatic: He requested exemption of guard colony rents and the construction of a princely residence.

sentences.zh: 許之。

translations.literal: This was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Both requests were granted.

sentences.zh: 遣主事毛俊經度，並建襄陵、樂平二邸及岷州廣福寺。

translations.literal: A principal clerk Mao Jun was sent to survey the site, and residences for Xiangling and Leping were also built, as well as the Guangfu Temple at Minzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Principal clerk Mao Jun was sent to survey the sites, and residences for the Xiangling and Leping lines were built, along with the Guangfu Temple at Minzhou.

sentences.zh: 陜西守臣言歲歉，請輟工。

translations.literal: The Shaanxi frontier officials reported a poor harvest and requested suspension of labor.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi frontier officials reported a poor harvest and asked that construction work be halted.

sentences.zh: 帝令繕王宮，罷建寺役。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered repair of the princely palace and abolished labor on temple construction.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered repairs to the princely palace and suspended work on the temple.

sentences.zh: 平涼接邊僥，間諜充斥，沖或習邊鄙利弊，正統元年上書極言邊事。

translations.literal: Pingliang adjoined the frontier; spies filled the region. Chongran was versed in the advantages and disadvantages of the borderlands, and in the first year of Zhengtong submitted a memorial speaking at length on frontier affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Pingliang lay on the frontier, where spies were everywhere. Chongran knew the border country well, and in the first year of the Zhengtong reign he submitted a memorial detailing frontier affairs at length.

sentences.zh: 賜書褒答。

translations.literal: An imperial letter of commendation was granted in reply.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent him a letter of commendation in reply.

sentences.zh: 五年薨。

translations.literal: He died in the fifth year.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth year of the Zhengtong reign.

sentences.zh: 子懷王範圯嗣，九年薨。

translations.literal: His son the Prince of Huai Fan Yi succeeded; he died in the ninth year.
translations.idiomatic: His son the Prince of Huai, Fan Yi, succeeded him and died in the ninth year.

sentences.zh: 弟靖王範仰嗣，景泰元年薨。

translations.literal: His younger brother the Prince of Jing Fan Yang succeeded; he died in the first year of Jingtai.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother the Prince of Jing, Fan Yang, succeeded and died in the first year of the Jingtai reign.

sentences.zh: 子惠王征釙嗣。

translations.literal: His son the Prince of Hui Zheng Bo succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son the Prince of Hui, Zheng Bo, succeeded.

sentences.zh: 初，土木之變，沖秌赴京師勤王，會解嚴。

translations.literal: At first, during the Tumu Crisis, Chongqiu went to the capital to rescue the throne, but the emergency was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during the Tumu Crisis, Chongqiu had set out for the capital to rescue the throne, but the crisis was resolved before he arrived.

sentences.zh: 下書慰勞。

translations.literal: An imperial letter of consolation and commendation was sent down.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent him a letter of consolation and commendation.

sentences.zh: 及成化六年，寇入河套，沖秌復請率子婿擊賊。

translations.literal: By the sixth year of Chenghua, when raiders entered the Ordos loop, Chongqiu again requested to lead his sons and sons-in-law to attack the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of the Chenghua reign, when raiders entered the Ordos loop, Chongqiu again asked to lead his sons and sons-in-law against them.

sentences.zh: 憲宗止之。

translations.literal: The Chenghua Emperor stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: The Chenghua Emperor refused the request.

sentences.zh: 沖或兄弟並急王事，以藩禁嚴不用。

translations.literal: Chongran and his brothers alike were eager to serve the throne, but because princely restrictions were strict they were not employed.
translations.idiomatic: Chongran and his brothers were all eager to serve the throne in military matters, but strict princely restrictions kept them from being used.

sentences.zh: 自是宗臣無預兵事者。

translations.literal: From this time onward no imperial clansmen took part in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After that, no member of the imperial clan was allowed to take part in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 成化五年，徵釙薨，子悼王偕㳘嗣，十年薨。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Chenghua Zheng Bo died; his son the Prince of Dao Xie Chong succeeded; he died in the tenth year.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Chenghua reign Zheng Bo died. His son the Prince of Dao, Xie Chong, succeeded him and died in the tenth year.

sentences.zh: 弟康王偕灊嗣，弘治十四年薨。

translations.literal: His younger brother the Prince of Kang Xie Qian succeeded; he died in the fourteenth year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother the Prince of Kang, Xie Qian, succeeded and died in the fourteenth year of the Hongzhi reign.

sentences.zh: 子昭王旭櫏嗣。

translations.literal: His son the Prince of Zhao Xu Gui succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son the Prince of Zhao, Xu Gui, succeeded.

sentences.zh: 性忠孝，工詩，居藩有惠政。

translations.literal: By nature loyal and filial, skilled in poetry, in his fief he had benevolent policies.
translations.idiomatic: He was loyal and filial by nature, skilled at poetry, and governed his fief with benevolent policies.

sentences.zh: 韓土瘠祿薄，弟建寧王旭㮁至，以所受金冊質於宗室偕泆，事聞，廢為庶人。

translations.literal: Han land was poor and stipends thin; his younger brother the Prince of Jianning Xu 㮁 arrived and pawned the golden patent he had received to the clansman Xie Yi; when the matter was reported, he was degraded to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: The Han fief was poor and its stipends meager. His younger brother the Prince of Jianning, Xu 㮁, pawned his golden patent of nobility to the clansman Xie Yi; when the matter came to light, he was stripped of rank and reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 諸貧宗往往淩劫有司，平涼知府吳世良、鄺衍、任守德、王松先後被窘辱。

translations.literal: Impoverished clansmen often bullied and robbed officials; the prefects of Pingliang Wu Shiliang, Kuang Yan, Ren Shoude, and Wang Song were successively harassed and humiliated.
translations.idiomatic: Impoverished clansmen often bullied and robbed local officials, and the prefects of Pingliang—Wu Shiliang, Kuang Yan, Ren Shoude, and Wang Song—were successively harassed and humiliated.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十三年，旭櫏薨。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Jiajing Xu Gui died.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Gui died in the thirteenth year of the Jiajing reign.

sentences.zh: 子定王融燧嗣，懲宗室之橫，頗繩以法。

translations.literal: His son the Prince of Ding Rong Sui succeeded; he punished the arrogance of the clansmen and restrained them rather strictly by law.
translations.idiomatic: His son the Prince of Ding, Rong Sui, succeeded and, to curb the arrogance of the clansmen, enforced the law on them with some rigor.

sentences.zh: 不逞者怨之。

translations.literal: The lawless resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Those who would not submit resented him.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，襄陵王融焚及諸宗二百余人訐奏王奸利事。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year the Prince of Xiangling Rong Fen and more than two hundred clansmen submitted accusations of the prince's corruption and self-interest.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year the Prince of Xiangling, Rong Fen, and more than two hundred other clansmen submitted accusations of corruption against the prince.

sentences.zh: 勘無實，革融焚等祿。

translations.literal: Investigation found no substance; the stipends of Rong Fen and the others were revoked.
translations.idiomatic: Investigation found no substance to the charges, and the stipends of Rong Fen and the others were revoked.

sentences.zh: 四十四年，融燧薨。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year Rong Sui died.
translations.idiomatic: Rong Sui died in the forty-fourth year of the Jiajing reign.

sentences.zh: 子謨㙉先卒。

translations.literal: His son Mo Dian died first.
translations.idiomatic: His son Mo Dian predeceased him.

sentences.zh: 世宗末年，以宗祿不足，詔身不及王者，許其嫡長子繼王，余子如故秩。

translations.literal: In the late years of the Jiajing Emperor, because imperial clan stipends were insufficient, an edict stated that those whose height did not reach princely standard might have their eldest legitimate sons succeed to the princely title, while the other sons kept their former ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Jiajing reign, because imperial clan stipends were insufficient, an edict allowed those who did not meet the height requirement for princes to have their eldest legitimate sons inherit the princely title, while other sons kept their former ranks.

sentences.zh: 謨㙉以世子不及王，王其長子朗锜，余子止鎮國將軍。

translations.literal: Because Mo Dian's heir did not reach princely height, his eldest son Lang Qi became prince, and the other sons remained only Defender-Generals of the State.
translations.idiomatic: Because Mo Dian's heir did not meet the height requirement, his eldest son Lang Qi inherited the princely title, while the other sons remained Defender-Generals of the State.

sentences.zh: 萬歷三十四年，朗锜薨，謚曰端。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year of Wanli Lang Qi died; his posthumous title was Duan.
translations.idiomatic: Lang Qi died in the thirty-fourth year of the Wanli reign and was posthumously titled Duan.

sentences.zh: 子孫皆早卒，曾孫亶塉嗣。

translations.literal: Sons and grandsons all died young; the great-grandson Dan Ji succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His sons and grandsons all died young, and succession passed to his great-grandson Dan Ji.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十六年，賊陷平涼，被執。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Chongzhen rebels captured Pingliang and he was taken prisoner.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year of the Chongzhen reign rebels captured Pingliang and took him prisoner.

sentences.zh: 襄陵王沖秌，憲王第二子，有至性。

translations.literal: The Prince of Xiangling Chongqiu, second son of the Prince of Xian, had exceptional character.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Xiangling, Chongqiu, second son of the Prince of Xian, was a man of exceptional character.

sentences.zh: 母病，刲股和藥，病良已。

translations.literal: When his mother fell ill, he cut flesh from his thigh and mixed it into medicine; the illness was fully cured.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother fell ill, he cut flesh from his thigh to mix into her medicine, and she recovered completely.

sentences.zh: 及卒，終喪毀瘠。

translations.literal: When she died, he completed the mourning period emaciated with grief.
translations.idiomatic: When she died, he observed the full mourning period and was wasted away with grief.

sentences.zh: 每展墓，必率子孫躬畚鍤培冢。

translations.literal: Whenever he tended the graves, he always led his descendants to personally take spade and basket and repair the tombs.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he tended the graves, he always led his descendants to personally shovel earth and repair the tombs.

sentences.zh: 先後璽書褒美者六。

translations.literal: Six imperial edicts of praise were sent in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Six imperial edicts of commendation were sent to him over the years.

sentences.zh: 子範址服其教，母荊罹危疾，亦刲股進之，愈。

translations.literal: His son Fan Zhi followed his teaching; when his mother Jing suffered a grave illness, he too cut flesh from his thigh and offered it to her, and she recovered.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fan Zhi followed his example; when his mother Jing fell gravely ill, he too cut flesh from his thigh for her, and she recovered.

sentences.zh: 其後五世同居，門內雍肅。

translations.literal: Afterward five generations lived together under one roof; within the household all was harmonious and solemn.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward five generations lived together under one roof, and the household was harmonious and dignified.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十一年賚以羊酒文幣。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Jiajing he was rewarded with sheep, wine, and ceremonial goods.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of the Jiajing reign he was rewarded with sheep, wine, and ceremonial gifts.

sentences.zh: 韓諸王以襄陵家法為第一。

translations.literal: Among the princes of Han, the Xiangling household's family discipline was ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: Among the Han princes, the Xiangling household's family discipline was considered the finest.

sentences.zh: 王孫征鑖病卒，聘杜氏女，未婚，歸王家，誌操甚歷，詔賜旌表。

translations.literal: The prince's grandson Zheng Shan died of illness; the Du family's daughter, betrothed to him though not yet married, returned to the Wang household and showed exceptional steadfastness of purpose; an edict granted her a commemorative plaque.
translations.idiomatic: The prince's grandson Zheng Shan died young. The Du family's daughter, though betrothed to him but not yet married, returned to the Wang household and showed exceptional virtue; the court granted her a commemorative plaque.

sentences.zh: 瀋簡王模，太祖第二十一子。

translations.literal: Prince Jian of Shen Mo, twenty-first son of the Taizu Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jian of Shen, Mo, was the twenty-first son of the Taizu Emperor.

sentences.zh: 洪武二十四年封。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed in the twenty-fourth year of Hongwu.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed in the twenty-fourth year of the Hongwu reign.

sentences.zh: 永樂六年就藩潞州。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yongle he went to his fief at Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of the Yongle reign he went to his fief at Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 宣德六年薨。

translations.literal: He died in the sixth year of Xuande.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth year of the Xuande reign.

sentences.zh: 子康王佶焞嗣。

translations.literal: His son the Prince of Kang Ji Chun succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son the Prince of Kang, Ji Chun, succeeded.

sentences.zh: 景泰中，數與州官置酒大會，巡撫朱鑒以聞。

translations.literal: During the Jingtai reign he repeatedly held great banquets with prefectural officials; Grand Coordinator Zhu Jian reported this.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingtai reign he repeatedly held lavish banquets with prefectural officials, and Grand Coordinator Zhu Jian reported the matter.

sentences.zh: 帝令諸王，非時令壽節，不得輒與有司宴飲，著為令。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the princes that except on seasonal festivals and birthdays they must not casually banquet and drink with officials, and this was established as a regulation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered that princes must not casually banquet with officials except on seasonal festivals and birthdays, and this was established as a permanent rule.

sentences.zh: 天順元年薨。

translations.literal: He died in the first year of Tianshun.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of the Tianshun reign.

sentences.zh: 子莊王幼學嗣，正德十一年薨。

translations.literal: His son the Prince of Zhuang You Xue succeeded; he died in the eleventh year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: His son the Prince of Zhuang, You Xue, succeeded and died in the eleventh year of the Zhengde reign.

sentences.zh: 子恭王詮鉦嗣，嘉靖六年薨。

translations.literal: His son the Prince of Gong Quan Zheng succeeded; he died in the sixth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: His son the Prince of Gong, Quan Zheng, succeeded and died in the sixth year of the Jiajing reign.

sentences.zh: 孫允榿攝府事，九年卒。

translations.literal: His grandson Yun Qi administered the princely estate and died in the ninth year.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Yun Qi administered the princely estate and died in the ninth year.

sentences.zh: 無子，再從弟憲王允栘攝府事，凡十年乃嗣封。

translations.literal: Having no son, his second cousin once removed the Prince of Xian Yun Yi administered the princely estate; only after ten years did he succeed to the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: He had no son, so his second cousin once removed, the Prince of Xian, Yun Yi, administered the estate for ten years before succeeding to the title.

sentences.zh: 當是時，瀋府諸郡王勛淯、詮並爭襲，帝皆切責之，而令允栘嗣。

translations.literal: At that time the commandery princes of the Shen princely line Xun Yu and Quan both contended for succession; the emperor sternly rebuked them both and ordered Yun Yi to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Shen commandery princes Xun Yu and Quan both contested the succession; the emperor sternly rebuked them and ordered Yun Yi to succeed.

sentences.zh: 二十八年薨。

translations.literal: He died in the twenty-eighth year.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twenty-eighth year of the Jiajing reign.

sentences.zh: 子宣王恬烄嗣，好學，工古文詞，審聲律。

translations.literal: His son the Prince of Xuan Tian Xu succeeded; he loved learning, was skilled in classical prose and poetry, and understood tonal rules.
translations.idiomatic: His son the Prince of Xuan, Tian Xu, succeeded. He loved learning, was skilled in classical prose and poetry, and had a fine ear for tonal rules.

sentences.zh: 弟安慶王恬爖、鎮康王恬焯，穆宗時皆以孝義旌。

translations.literal: His younger brothers the Princes of Anqing Tian Lian and Zhenkang Tian Chao were both honored for filial piety and righteousness during the Muzong reign.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brothers the Princes of Anqing, Tian Lian, and Zhenkang, Tian Chao, were both honored for filial piety during the Muzong reign.

sentences.zh: 萬歷十年，恬烄薨。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Wanli Tian Xu died.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Xu died in the tenth year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 子定王呈堯嗣，仁孝恭慎。

translations.literal: His son the Prince of Ding Cheng Yao succeeded; he was benevolent, filial, respectful, and cautious.
translations.idiomatic: His son the Prince of Ding, Cheng Yao, succeeded. He was benevolent, filial, respectful, and cautious.

sentences.zh: 弟六人，封郡王者二。

translations.literal: He had six younger brothers; two were enfeoffed as commandery princes.
translations.idiomatic: He had six younger brothers, of whom two were enfeoffed as commandery princes.

sentences.zh: 余例不得封，朝廷獎王恭，皆封郡王而不與祿。

translations.literal: The rest by precedent could not be enfeoffed; the court rewarded the prince's humility, enfeoffing them all as commandery princes but without stipends.
translations.idiomatic: The rest could not be enfeoffed by precedent, but the court rewarded the prince's humility by granting them all commandery prince titles without stipends.

sentences.zh: 薨，子效鏞嗣，明亡，國除。

translations.literal: He died; his son Xiao Yong succeeded; when the Ming fell, the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was succeeded by his son Xiao Yong; when the Ming dynasty fell, the princely state was abolished.

sentences.zh: 沁水王呈堦、簡王七世孫也，工詩喜士，名譽藉甚。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qinshui Cheng Jie was a seventh-generation descendant of Prince Jian; skilled in poetry and fond of scholars, his reputation was very great.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qinshui, Cheng Jie, was a seventh-generation descendant of Prince Jian. Skilled at poetry and fond of scholars, he enjoyed great renown.

sentences.zh: 前此，有德平王允梃負俊才，與衡府新樂王載璽，周宗人睦㮮、俊噤等齊名。

translations.literal: Before this the Prince of Deping Yun Ting possessed outstanding talent and was equally famed with the Prince of Xinle Zai Xi of the Heng princely line and the Zhou clansmen Mu Xian and Jun Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Prince of Deping, Yun Ting, possessed outstanding talent and was ranked alongside the Prince of Xinle, Zai Xi, of the Heng princely line and the Zhou clansmen Mu Xian and Jun Jin.

sentences.zh: 又清源王幼㘧，康王第三子，博學能文詞。

translations.literal: Also the Prince of Qingyuan You Chu, third son of the Prince of Kang, was broadly learned and skilled in literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: There was also the Prince of Qingyuan, You Chu, third son of the Prince of Kang, who was broadly learned and skilled in literary composition.

sentences.zh: 其後，輔國將軍勛漣，從子允杉、允檸、允析，及鎮國將軍恬烷與諸子呈圻等，並以能詩名，時稱瀋藩多才焉。

translations.literal: Afterward Supporter-General of the State Xun Lian, his grandnephews Yun Shan, Yun Ning, and Yun Xi, and Defender-General of the State Tian Wan with his sons Cheng Qi and others were all famed for poetry; the age called the Shen princely line rich in talent.
translations.idiomatic: Later, Supporter-General of the State Xun Lian, his grandnephews Yun Shan, Yun Ning, and Yun Xi, and Defender-General of the State Tian Wan and his sons Cheng Qi and others were all famed for poetry; people of the time said the Shen princely line abounded in talent.

sentences.zh: 安惠王楹，太祖第二十二子。

translations.literal: Prince Hui of An Ying, twenty-second son of the Taizu Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Hui of An, Ying, was the twenty-second son of the Taizu Emperor.

sentences.zh: 洪武二十四年封。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed in the twenty-fourth year of Hongwu.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed in the twenty-fourth year of the Hongwu reign.

sentences.zh: 永樂六年就藩平涼。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yongle he went to his fief at Pingliang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of the Yongle reign he went to his fief at Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 十五年薨。

translations.literal: He died in the fifteenth year.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifteenth year of the Yongle reign.

sentences.zh: 無子，封除。

translations.literal: Having no son, the enfeoffment was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: He had no son, and the enfeoffment was abolished.

sentences.zh: 府僚及樂戶悉罷，留典仗校尉百人守園。

translations.literal: The princely staff and musician households were all dismissed; a hundred ceremonial guard officers were retained to guard the estate.
translations.idiomatic: The princely staff and musician households were all dismissed, and a hundred ceremonial guard officers were retained to guard the estate.

sentences.zh: 洪熙初，韓恭王改封平涼，就安王邸。

translations.literal: Early in the Hongxi reign the Prince of Gong of Han was reassigned to Pingliang and took residence at the An princely mansion.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Hongxi reign the Prince of Gong of Han was reassigned to Pingliang and took up residence at the An princely mansion.

sentences.zh: 英宗令官校隸韓，長史供安王祀，暇日給韓王子襄陵王沖秌使令。

translations.literal: The Yingzong Emperor ordered the guard officers subordinated to Han; the chief steward maintained sacrifices to the An prince, and on idle days supplied them to Chongqiu, Prince of Xiangling and son of the Han prince, for his service.
translations.idiomatic: The Yingzong Emperor ordered the guard officers placed under Han's authority; the chief steward maintained sacrifices to the An prince, and on free days supplied them to Chongqiu, the Prince of Xiangling and son of the Han prince, for his use.

sentences.zh: 景泰五年，沖秌遂乞承安王祀。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jingtai Chongqiu then requested to undertake sacrifices to the An prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Jingtai reign Chongqiu requested permission to undertake sacrifices to the An prince.

sentences.zh: 正德十二年嗣襄陵王征鈐，請樂戶祀安王。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Zhengde the succeeding Prince of Xiangling Zheng Qian requested musician households for sacrifices to the An prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of the Zhengde reign the succeeding Prince of Xiangling, Zheng Qian, requested musician households to perform sacrifices to the An prince.

sentences.zh: 明年，樂平王征錏援征鈐例以請。

translations.literal: The next year the Prince of Leping Zheng Yin cited Zheng Qian's precedent in making the request.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the Prince of Leping, Zheng Yin, cited Zheng Qian's precedent in making the same request.

sentences.zh: 禮部言：「親王有樂戶。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Rites stated: "Princes of the first rank have musician households.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites stated: "Princes of the first rank have musician households.

sentences.zh: 郡王別城居者，有事假鼓吹於有司。

translations.literal: Commandery princes residing in separate cities, when they have need, borrow ceremonial musicians from officials.
translations.idiomatic: Commandery princes who live in separate cities may borrow ceremonial musicians from local officials when needed.

sentences.zh: 其附親王國者，假樂戶於長史司。」

translations.literal: Those attached to a princely state borrow musician households from the chief steward's office."
translations.idiomatic: Those attached to a princely state must borrow musician households from the chief steward's office."

sentences.zh: 因並革安王供祀樂戶。

translations.literal: Accordingly they also abolished the musician households maintained for sacrifices to the An prince.
translations.idiomatic: On that basis they also abolished the musician households maintained for sacrifices to the An prince.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二年，韓王旭櫏復為代請。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiajing the Han prince Xu Gui again requested on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Jiajing reign the Han prince Xu Gui again petitioned on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 帝以安王故，報可之。

translations.literal: The emperor, for the An prince's sake, approved the request.
translations.idiomatic: For the An prince's sake, the emperor approved the request.

sentences.zh: 征鈐卒，韓王融燧令長史革之。

translations.literal: When Zheng Qian died, the Han prince Rong Sui ordered the chief steward to abolish them.
translations.idiomatic: When Zheng Qian died, the Han prince Rong Sui ordered the chief steward to abolish the musician households.

sentences.zh: 征鈐長孫旭橦上言：「禮樂自天子出，韓王不宜擅予奪。」

translations.literal: Zheng Qian's eldest grandson Xu Tang memorialized: "Rites and music issue from the Son of Heaven; the Han prince should not arbitrarily grant or revoke them."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Qian's eldest grandson Xu Tang memorialized: "Rites and music issue from the Son of Heaven; the Han prince should not grant or revoke them on his own authority."

sentences.zh: 融燧亦言：「親王、郡王禮樂宜有降殺。」

translations.literal: Rong Sui also stated: "Princes of the first and second rank should have graduated rites and music."
translations.idiomatic: Rong Sui also stated: "Princes of the first and second rank should receive rites and music in graduated form."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「樂戶為安王祀也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The musician households are for sacrifices to the An prince."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "The musician households are for sacrifices to the An prince."

sentences.zh: 給如故。

translations.literal: They were provisioned as before.
translations.idiomatic: They were provisioned as before.

sentences.zh: 唐定王桱，太祖第二十三子。

translations.literal: Prince Ding of Tang Jing, twenty-third son of the Taizu Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ding of Tang, Jing, was the twenty-third son of the Taizu Emperor.

sentences.zh: 洪武二十四年封。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed in the twenty-fourth year of Hongwu.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed in the twenty-fourth year of the Hongwu reign.

sentences.zh: 永樂六年就藩南陽。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yongle he went to his fief at Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of the Yongle reign he went to his fief at Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 十三年薨。

translations.literal: He died in the thirteenth year.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the thirteenth year of the Yongle reign.

sentences.zh: 子靖王瓊烴嗣。

translations.literal: His son the Prince of Jing Qiong Huan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son the Prince of Jing, Qiong Huan, succeeded.

sentences.zh: 綜核有矩矱，為成祖所喜。

translations.literal: He managed affairs within proper bounds and was favored by the Chengzu Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: He managed affairs with proper restraint and was favored by the Chengzu Emperor.

sentences.zh: 入朝，五日三召見。

translations.literal: On visiting court, within five days he was summoned to audience three times.
translations.idiomatic: When he came to court, he was summoned to audience three times in five days.

sentences.zh: 宣德元年薨。

translations.literal: He died in the first year of Xuande.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of the Xuande reign.

sentences.zh: 妃高氏未冊，自經以殉，詔封靖王妃。

translations.literal: Consort Gao, not yet formally invested, hanged herself to follow him in death; an edict enfeoffed her as consort of the Prince of Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Gao, not yet formally invested as princess consort, hanged herself to follow him in death, and an edict enfeoffed her as consort of the Prince of Jing.

sentences.zh: 無子，弟憲王瓊炟嗣，成化十一年薨。

translations.literal: Having no son, his younger brother the Prince of Xian Qiong Ta succeeded; he died in the eleventh year of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: He had no son, so his younger brother the Prince of Xian, Qiong Ta, succeeded and died in the eleventh year of the Chenghua reign.

sentences.zh: 子莊王芝址嗣，諸弟三城王芝垝、蕩陰王芝瓦並好學，有令譽。

translations.literal: His son the Prince of Zhuang Zhi Zhi succeeded; his younger brothers the Princes of Sancheng Zhi Gui and Tangyin Zhi Wa were all devoted to learning and had excellent reputations.
translations.idiomatic: His son the Prince of Zhuang, Zhi Zhi, succeeded. His younger brothers the Princes of Sancheng, Zhi Gui, and Tangyin, Zhi Wa, were all devoted scholars with excellent reputations.

sentences.zh: 而承休王芝垠，憲王繼妃焦氏子也，妃愛之。

translations.literal: As for the Prince of Chengxia Zhi Yin, he was the son of Prince Xian's secondary consort Lady Jiao; the consort doted on him.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Chengxia, Zhi Yin, was the son of the Prince of Xian's secondary consort, Lady Jiao, whom the consort favored above all.

sentences.zh: 遇節旦，召樂婦入宮。

translations.literal: On festival days he summoned female musicians into the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On festival days he would summon female musicians into the palace.

sentences.zh: 芝址詰之，語不遜。

translations.literal: Zhi Zhi questioned him, and his words were insolent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Zhi questioned him, but his replies were insolent.

sentences.zh: 焦妃怒，持鐵錘擊宮門，芝址閉不敢出。

translations.literal: Consort Jiao grew angry, took an iron hammer and struck the palace gate; Zhi Zhi shut himself in and dared not come out.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Jiao flew into a rage, took an iron hammer, and struck the palace gate; Zhi Zhi shut himself in and dared not emerge.

sentences.zh: 芝垠與妃弟璟誣王詈繼母。

translations.literal: Zhi Yin and the consort's younger brother Jing falsely accused the prince of cursing his stepmother.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Yin and the consort's younger brother Jing falsely accused the prince of reviling his stepmother.

sentences.zh: 按驗不實，得芝垠慢母詈兄狀，革爵。

translations.literal: Investigation found the charge untrue, but established that Zhi Yin had been disrespectful to his mother and abusive toward his elder brother; his title was revoked.
translations.idiomatic: Investigation proved the charge false, but established that Zhi Yin had been disrespectful to his mother and abusive toward his elder brother, and his title was revoked.

sentences.zh: 久之始復。

translations.literal: Only after a long time was it restored.
translations.idiomatic: Only after a long interval was it restored.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，芝址薨。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, Zhi Zhi died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year, Zhi Zhi died.

sentences.zh: 子成王彌鍗嗣。

translations.literal: His son the Prince of Cheng Mi Jin succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son the Prince of Cheng, Mi Jin, succeeded.

sentences.zh: 弘治中，疏言：「朝廷待親藩，生爵歿謚，親親至矣。

translations.literal: During the Hongzhi reign he submitted a memorial saying: "The court's treatment of princely relatives— granting titles in life and posthumous names in death— embodies the utmost devotion to kinship.
translations.idiomatic: During the Hongzhi reign he submitted a memorial saying: "In its treatment of princely kin, the court grants titles in life and posthumous names in death— kinship devotion could go no further.

sentences.zh: 間有惡未敗聞，歿獲美謚，是使善者怠，惡者肆也。

translations.literal: Yet sometimes those whose wickedness has not yet been exposed receive fine posthumous names after death, which makes the good grow lax and the wicked reckless.
translations.idiomatic: Yet sometimes men whose wickedness has not yet come to light receive fine posthumous names after death, which makes the good grow lax and the wicked reckless.

sentences.zh: 自今宜勘實，用寓彰癉。」

translations.literal: From now on facts should be verified, thereby manifesting reward and reproof."
translations.idiomatic: From now on the facts should be verified, thereby manifesting reward and reproof."

sentences.zh: 禮臣請降敕獎諭，勉勵諸王。

translations.literal: The minister of rites requested that an edict of commendation be issued to encourage all the princes.
translations.idiomatic: The minister of rites requested that an edict of commendation be issued to encourage and exhort all the princes.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The edict was approved.

sentences.zh: 武宗喜遊幸，彌鍗作《憂國詩》，且上疏以用賢圖治為言。

translations.literal: The Wuzong Emperor loved touring and hunting; Mi Jin composed "Poems of Concern for the State" and submitted a memorial urging the employment of worthies and pursuit of good governance.
translations.idiomatic: The Wuzong Emperor loved touring and hunting; Mi Jin composed Poems of Concern for the State and submitted a memorial urging the employment of worthies and the pursuit of good governance.

sentences.zh: 弟文城王彌鉗有學行，孝友篤至。

translations.literal: His younger brother the Prince of Wencheng Mi Qian was a man of learning and conduct, filial and brotherly to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother the Prince of Wencheng, Mi Qian, was a man of learning and upright conduct, filial and brotherly to the utmost.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二年，彌鍗薨。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiajing, Mi Jin died.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Jiajing reign, Mi Jin died.

sentences.zh: 無子，彌鉗子敬王宇溫嗣。

translations.literal: Having no son, Mi Qian's son the Prince of Jing Yu Wen succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: He had no son, so Mi Qian's son the Prince of Jing, Yu Wen, succeeded.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，獻金助太廟工，賜玉帶，益祿二百石。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he contributed gold toward work on the ancestral temple, was granted a jade belt, and had his stipend increased by two hundred shi.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he contributed gold toward work on the ancestral temple, was granted a jade belt, and received an increase of two hundred shi to his stipend.

sentences.zh: 時承休王芝垠子彌鋠以父與莊王交訐，失令名，折節蓋前愆。

translations.literal: At the time the Prince of Chengxia Zhi Yin's son Mi Chen, because his father had quarreled with the Prince of Zhuang and lost a fine reputation, had reformed his conduct to atone for past faults.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Prince of Chengxia Zhi Yin's son Mi Chen, whose father had quarreled with the Prince of Zhuang and lost a fine reputation, had reformed his conduct to atone for past faults.

sentences.zh: 宇溫上其事。

translations.literal: Yu Wen reported this to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Wen reported this to the throne.

sentences.zh: 璽書褒獎。

translations.literal: An imperial letter of commendation was sent.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial letter of commendation was sent.

sentences.zh: 三十九年，宇溫薨。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year, Yu Wen died.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-ninth year, Yu Wen died.

sentences.zh: 子順王宙栐嗣，四十三年薨。

translations.literal: His son the Prince of Shun Zhou Bing succeeded and died in the forty-third year.
translations.idiomatic: His son the Prince of Shun, Zhou Bing, succeeded and died in the forty-third year.

sentences.zh: 子端王碩熿嗣。

translations.literal: His son the Prince of Duan Shuo Huang succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son the Prince of Duan, Shuo Huang, succeeded.

sentences.zh: 惑於嬖人，囚世子器墭及其子聿鍵於承奉司，器墭中毒死。

translations.literal: Beguiled by a favorite, he imprisoned the heir Qi Bao and his son Yu Jian in the Office of Attendance; Qi Bao died by poison.
translations.idiomatic: Beguiled by a favorite, he imprisoned the heir Qi Bao and his son Yu Jian in the Office of Attendance; Qi Bao died of poison.

sentences.zh: 崇禎五年，碩熿薨，聿鍵嗣。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Chongzhen, Shuo Huang died and Yu Jian succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Chongzhen reign, Shuo Huang died and Yu Jian succeeded.

sentences.zh: 七年，流賊大熾，蠲金築南陽城，又援潞藩例，乞增兵三千人。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, with bandits raging, he remitted funds to build the walls of Nanyang and, citing the precedent of the Prince of Lu, requested three thousand additional troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, as bandit armies swelled, he remitted funds to build the walls of Nanyang and, citing the precedent of the Prince of Lu, requested three thousand additional troops.

sentences.zh: 不許。

translations.literal: The request was denied.
translations.idiomatic: The request was denied.

sentences.zh: 九年秋八月，京師戒嚴，倡義勤王。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of autumn in the ninth year, when the capital was placed under martial law, he raised troops in a righteous march to aid the throne.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of autumn in the ninth year, when the capital was placed under martial law, he raised troops in a righteous march to aid the throne.

sentences.zh: 詔切責，勒還國。

translations.literal: An edict sharply rebuked him and ordered him back to his fief.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sharply rebuked him and ordered him back to his fief.

sentences.zh: 事定，下部議，廢為庶人，幽之鳳陽。

translations.literal: When matters settled, the case was referred to the ministries for deliberation; he was degraded to commoner status and confined at Fengyang.
translations.idiomatic: When the crisis passed, the case was referred to the ministries for deliberation; he was degraded to commoner status and confined at Fengyang.

sentences.zh: 弟聿鏌嗣。

translations.literal: His younger brother Yu Mo succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Yu Mo succeeded.

sentences.zh: 十四年，李自成陷南陽，聿鏌遇害。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, when Li Zicheng took Nanyang, Yu Mo was killed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, when Li Zicheng took Nanyang, Yu Mo was killed.

sentences.zh: 十七年，京師陷，福王由崧立於南京，乃赦聿鍵出。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, after the capital fell, the Prince of Fu, You Song, was enthroned at Nanjing and Yu Jian was pardoned and released.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, after the capital fell, the Prince of Fu, You Song, was enthroned at Nanjing, and Yu Jian was pardoned and released.

sentences.zh: 大清順治二年五月，南都降。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the second year of Shunzhi under the Great Qing, the Southern Capital surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the second year of Shunzhi under the Great Qing, the Southern Capital surrendered.

sentences.zh: 聿鍵行至杭，遇鎮江總兵官鄭鴻逵、戶部郎中蘇觀生，遂奉入閩。

translations.literal: Yu Jian traveled as far as Hangzhou, where he met the regional commander of Zhenjiang, Zheng Hongkui, and the Court of Revenue bureau director Su Guansheng, and was escorted into Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jian traveled as far as Hangzhou, where he met the regional commander of Zhenjiang, Zheng Hongkui, and the Court of Revenue bureau director Su Guansheng, and was escorted into Fujian.

sentences.zh: 南安伯鄭芝龍、巡撫都御史張肯堂與禮部尚書黃道周等定議，奉王稱監國。

translations.literal: The Marquis of Nan'an, Zheng Zhilong, the grand coordinator and censor-in-chief Zhang Kentang, and the minister of rites Huang Daozhou and others decided to install the prince as regent.
translations.idiomatic: The Marquis of Nan'an, Zheng Zhilong, the grand coordinator and censor-in-chief Zhang Kentang, and the minister of rites Huang Daozhou and others decided to install the prince as regent.

sentences.zh: 閏六月丁未，遂立於福州，號隆武，改福州為天興府。

translations.literal: On dingwei day in the intercalary sixth month he was enthroned at Fuzhou under the era name Longwu, and Fuzhou was renamed Tianxing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei day in the intercalary sixth month he was enthroned at Fuzhou under the era name Longwu, and Fuzhou was renamed Tianxing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 進芝龍、鴻逵為侯，封鄭芝豹、鄭彩為伯，觀生、道周俱大學士，肯堂為兵部尚書，余拜官有差。

translations.literal: Zhilong and Hongkui were advanced to marquis; Zheng Zhibao and Zheng Cai were enfeoffed as earls; Guansheng and Daozhou were both made grand secretaries; Kentang was made minister of war; and the others received appointments according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: Zhilong and Hongkui were advanced to marquis; Zheng Zhibao and Zheng Cai were enfeoffed as earls; Guansheng and Daozhou were both made grand secretaries; Kentang was made minister of war; and the others received appointments according to rank.

sentences.zh: 聿鍵好學，通典故，然權在鄭氏，不能有所為。

translations.literal: Yu Jian loved learning and was versed in precedent, yet power lay with the Zheng clan and he could accomplish nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jian loved learning and was versed in precedent, yet power lay with the Zheng clan and he could accomplish nothing.

sentences.zh: 是年八月，芝龍議簡戰守兵二十余萬，計餉不支其半。

translations.literal: That August, Zhilong proposed to select lean combat and garrison forces of more than two hundred thousand men, but estimated supplies would not cover even half.
translations.idiomatic: That August, Zhilong proposed to muster more than two hundred thousand combat and garrison troops, but estimated that supplies would cover less than half their needs.

sentences.zh: 請預借兩稅一年，令群下捐俸，勸紳士輸助，征府縣銀谷未解者。

translations.literal: He requested advance collection of both tax levies for one year, ordered officials to donate salaries, urged gentry to contribute, and collected silver and grain from prefectures and counties not yet remitted.
translations.idiomatic: He requested advance collection of both tax levies for one year, ordered officials to donate their salaries, urged gentry to contribute, and collected silver and grain from prefectures and counties that had not yet remitted payment.

sentences.zh: 官吏督迫，閭裏騷然。

translations.literal: Officials pressed collection and the neighborhoods were in uproar.
translations.idiomatic: Officials pressed collection relentlessly, and the neighborhoods were in uproar.

sentences.zh: 又廣開事例，猶苦不足。

translations.literal: Special sale offices were opened widely, yet funds still fell short.
translations.idiomatic: Sale of offices by special precedent was opened widely, yet funds still fell short.

sentences.zh: 仙霞嶺守關兵僅數百人，皆不堪用。

translations.literal: The border garrison at Xianxia Pass numbered only a few hundred men, all unfit for service.
translations.idiomatic: The border garrison at Xianxia Pass numbered only a few hundred men, all unfit for service.

sentences.zh: 聿鍵屢促芝龍出兵，輒以餉詘辭。

translations.literal: Yu Jian repeatedly urged Zhilong to take the field, but he always pleaded shortage of supplies.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jian repeatedly urged Zhilong to take the field, but Zhilong always pleaded shortage of supplies.

sentences.zh: 久之，芝龍知眾論不平，乃請以鴻逵出浙東，彩出江西，各擁兵數千，號數萬。

translations.literal: After some time, knowing public opinion was hostile, Zhilong proposed that Hongkui advance into eastern Zhejiang and Cai into Jiangxi, each leading several thousand troops while claiming tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: After some time, knowing public opinion was hostile, Zhilong proposed that Hongkui advance into eastern Zhejiang and Cai into Jiangxi, each leading several thousand troops while claiming tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 既行，托候餉，皆行百里而還。

translations.literal: Once they had set out, they pleaded waiting for supplies and each marched a hundred li before returning.
translations.idiomatic: Once they had set out, they pleaded that they were awaiting supplies and each marched a hundred li before turning back.

sentences.zh: 先是，黃道周知芝龍無意出師，自請行，從廣信趨婺源，兵潰死，事詳《道周傳》。

translations.literal: Earlier, Huang Daozhou, knowing Zhilong had no intention of campaigning, had volunteered to go himself; marching from Guangxin toward Wuyuan, his army was routed and he died—the affair is detailed in the "Biography of Daozhou."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Huang Daozhou, knowing Zhilong had no intention of taking the field, had volunteered to go himself; marching from Guangxin toward Wuyuan, his army was routed and he was killed—the affair is detailed in the Biography of Daozhou.

sentences.zh: 是時，李自成兵敗，走死通山。

translations.literal: At this time Li Zicheng's forces were defeated; he fled and died at Tongshan.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Li Zicheng's forces were defeated; he fled and died at Tongshan.

sentences.zh: 其兄子李錦帥眾降於湖廣總督何騰蛟，一時增兵十余萬。

translations.literal: His nephew Li Jin led the remnant host in surrender to the Huguang governor-general He Tengjiao, suddenly adding more than a hundred thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Li Jin led the remnant host in surrender to the Huguang governor-general He Tengjiao, suddenly adding more than a hundred thousand troops to the cause.

sentences.zh: 侍郎楊廷麟、祭酒劉同升起兵復吉安、臨江。

translations.literal: Vice-minister Yang Tinglin and libationer Liu Tongqi raised troops and recovered Ji'an and Linjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Vice-minister Yang Tinglin and libationer Liu Tongqi raised troops and recovered Ji'an and Linjiang.

sentences.zh: 於是廷麟等請聿鍵出江右，騰蛟請出湖南。

translations.literal: Thereupon Tinglin and others urged Yu Jian to advance into Jiangxi, and Tengjiao urged him into Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Tinglin and others urged Yu Jian to advance into Jiangxi, and Tengjiao urged him to advance into Hunan.

sentences.zh: 原任知州金堡言騰蛟可恃，芝龍不可恃，宜棄閩就楚。

translations.literal: Former prefect Jin Bao said Tengjiao could be relied upon but Zhilong could not, and that they should abandon Fujian for Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Former prefect Jin Bao said Tengjiao could be relied upon but Zhilong could not, and that they should abandon Fujian for the Chu region.

sentences.zh: 聿鍵大喜，授堡給事中，遣觀生先行募兵。

translations.literal: Yu Jian was greatly pleased; he made Bao a supervising secretary and sent Guansheng ahead to raise troops.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jian was greatly pleased; he made Bao a supervising secretary and sent Guansheng ahead to raise troops.

sentences.zh: 先是，靖江王亨嘉僭稱監國，不奉聿鍵命，為巡撫瞿式耜等所擒，以捷聞。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Prince of Jingjiang, Heng Jia, had usurped the title of regent and refused Yu Jian's orders; he was captured by the grand coordinator Qu Shisi and others, and victory was reported.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Prince of Jingjiang, Heng Jia, had usurped the title of regent and refused to obey Yu Jian; he was captured by the grand coordinator Qu Shisi and others, and victory was reported.

sentences.zh: 而魯王以海又稱監國於紹興，拒聿鍵使者，故聿鍵決意出江西、湖廣。

translations.literal: Meanwhile the Prince of Lu, Yihai, also styled himself regent at Shaoxing and rejected Yu Jian's envoys; hence Yu Jian resolved to advance into Jiangxi and Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile the Prince of Lu, Yihai, also styled himself regent at Shaoxing and rejected Yu Jian's envoys; hence Yu Jian resolved to advance into Jiangxi and Huguang.

sentences.zh: 十二月發福州，駐建寧。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he departed Fuzhou and encamped at Jianning.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he departed Fuzhou and encamped at Jianning.

sentences.zh: 廣東布政湯來賀運餉十萬，由海道至。

translations.literal: Guangdong administration commissioner Tang Laihe transported one hundred thousand in supplies by sea.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong administration commissioner Tang Laihe transported one hundred thousand in supplies by sea.

sentences.zh: 明年二月駐延平。

translations.literal: In the second month of the following year he encamped at Yanping.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the following year he encamped at Yanping.

sentences.zh: 三月，大清兵取吉安、撫州，圍楊廷麟於贛州。

translations.literal: In the third month Qing forces took Ji'an and Fuzhou and besieged Yang Tinglin at Ganzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Qing forces took Ji'an and Fuzhou and besieged Yang Tinglin at Ganzhou.

sentences.zh: 尚書郭維經出閩，募兵援贛。

translations.literal: Minister Guo Weijing left Fujian to raise troops and relieve Ganzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Guo Weijing left Fujian to raise troops and relieve Ganzhou.

sentences.zh: 六月，大兵克紹興，魯王以海遁入海，閩中大震。

translations.literal: In the sixth month the great army took Shaoxing; the Prince of Lu, Yihai, fled by sea, and all Fujian was shaken.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the great army took Shaoxing; the Prince of Lu, Yihai, fled by sea, and all Fujian was shaken.

sentences.zh: 芝龍假言海寇至，徹兵回安平鎮，航海去。

translations.literal: Zhilong falsely claimed sea pirates had arrived, withdrew his troops to Anpingzhen, and sailed away.
translations.idiomatic: Zhilong falsely claimed sea pirates had arrived, withdrew his troops to Anping Town, and sailed away.

sentences.zh: 守關將士皆隨之，仙霞嶺空無一人。

translations.literal: The garrison at the pass followed him all; Xianxia Pass was left utterly empty.
translations.idiomatic: The border garrison followed him entirely, and Xianxia Pass was left utterly empty.

sentences.zh: 七月，何騰蛟遣使迎聿鍵，將至韶州。

translations.literal: In the seventh month He Tengjiao sent envoys to welcome Yu Jian, who was approaching Shaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month He Tengjiao sent envoys to welcome Yu Jian, who was approaching Shaozhou.

sentences.zh: 唯時我兵已抵閩關，守浦城御史鄭為虹、給事中黃大鵬、延平知府王士和死焉。

translations.literal: But by then Qing forces had already reached the Fujian border; the censor of Pucheng, Zheng Weihong, the supervising secretary Huang Dapeng, and the prefect of Yanping, Wang Shihe, all died there.
translations.idiomatic: But by then Qing forces had already reached the Fujian border; the censor of Pucheng, Zheng Weihong, the supervising secretary Huang Dapeng, and the prefect of Yanping, Wang Shihe, all died defending the pass.

sentences.zh: 八月，聿鍵出走，數日方至汀州。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Yu Jian fled; only after several days did he reach Tingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Yu Jian fled; only after several days did he reach Tingzhou.

sentences.zh: 大兵奄至，從官奔散，與妃曾氏俱被執。

translations.literal: The great army suddenly arrived; his attendants scattered, and he and Consort Zeng were both captured.
translations.idiomatic: The great army suddenly arrived; his attendants scattered, and he and Consort Zeng were both captured.

sentences.zh: 妃至九瀧投於水，聿鍵死於福州。

translations.literal: The consort, reaching Jiulong, threw herself into the water; Yu Jian died at Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The consort, reaching Jiulong Rapids, threw herself into the water; Yu Jian died at Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 給事中熊緯、尚書曹學佺、通政使馬思禮等自縊死。

translations.literal: Supervising secretary Xiong Wei, minister Cao Xuequan, transmission commissioner Ma Sili, and others hanged themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Xiong Wei, minister Cao Xuequan, transmission commissioner Ma Sili, and others hanged themselves.

sentences.zh: 郢靖王棟，太祖第二十四子。

translations.literal: Prince Jing of Ying, Dong, was the twenty-fourth son of the Taizu Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jing of Ying, Dong, was the twenty-fourth son of the Taizu Emperor.

sentences.zh: 洪武二十四年封。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed in the twenty-fourth year of Hongwu.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed in the twenty-fourth year of the Hongwu reign.

sentences.zh: 永樂六年之藩安陸。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yongle he went to his fief at Anlu.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of the Yongle reign he went to his fief at Anlu.

sentences.zh: 十二年薨。

translations.literal: He died in the twelfth year.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twelfth year of the Yongle reign.

sentences.zh: 無子封除。

translations.literal: Having no son, the enfeoffment was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Having no son, the enfeoffment was abolished.

sentences.zh: 留內外官校守園。

translations.literal: Inner and outer officials and guards were left to keep the estate.
translations.idiomatic: Inner and outer officials and guards were left to maintain the estate.

sentences.zh: 王妃郭氏，武定侯英女。

translations.literal: The princess consort was Lady Guo, daughter of the Marquis of Wuding, Ying.
translations.idiomatic: The princess consort was Lady Guo, daughter of the Marquis of Wuding, Ying.

sentences.zh: 王薨逾月，妃慟哭曰：「未亡人無子，尚誰恃？」

translations.literal: More than a month after the prince's death, the consort wailed and said: "This widow has no son— upon whom can I still rely?"
