translations.idiomatic: More than a month after the prince's death, the consort wailed and said: "This widow has no son— upon whom can I still rely?"

sentences.zh: 引鏡寫容付宮人，曰：「俟諸女長，令識母。」

translations.literal: She had her likeness taken in a mirror and entrusted it to a palace woman, saying: "When my daughters are grown, let them know their mother."
translations.idiomatic: She had her likeness painted from a mirror and entrusted it to a palace woman, saying: "When my daughters are grown, let them know their mother."

sentences.zh: 遂自經。

translations.literal: Then she hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: Then she hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 妃四女，一夭，其三女封光化、穀城、南漳郡主，歲祿各八百石。

translations.literal: The consort had four daughters; one died young; the other three were enfeoffed as commandery princesses of Guanghua, Gucheng, and Nanzhang, each with an annual stipend of eight hundred shi.
translations.idiomatic: The consort had four daughters; one died young; the other three were enfeoffed as commandery princesses of Guanghua, Gucheng, and Nanzhang, each with an annual stipend of eight hundred shi.

sentences.zh: 宣德四年，以郢故邸封梁王瞻垍，移郢宮人居南京。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xuande, the former residence of Ying was used to enfeoff the Prince of Liang, Zhan Ji, and the Ying palace household was moved to Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the Xuande reign, the former residence of Ying was used to enfeoff the Prince of Liang, Zhan Ji, and the Ying palace household was moved to Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 伊歷王，太祖第二十五子。

translations.literal: Prince Li of Yi was the twenty-fifth son of the Taizu Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Li of Yi was the twenty-fifth son of the Taizu Emperor.

sentences.zh: 洪武二十一年生，生四年封。

translations.literal: Born in the twenty-first year of Hongwu, he was enfeoffed in the fourth year of his life.
translations.idiomatic: Born in the twenty-first year of the Hongwu reign, he was enfeoffed in the fourth year of his life.

sentences.zh: 永樂六年之藩洛陽，歲祿僅二千石。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yongle he went to his fief at Luoyang, with an annual stipend of only two thousand shi.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of the Yongle reign he went to his fief at Luoyang, with an annual stipend of only two thousand shi.

sentences.zh: 王好武，不樂居宮中，時時挾彈露劍，馳逐郊外。

translations.literal: The prince loved martial arts and disliked living within the palace; he would often carry a crossbow, bare his sword, and gallop in pursuit outside the city.
translations.idiomatic: The prince loved martial arts and disliked living within the palace; he would often carry a crossbow, bare his sword, and gallop in pursuit outside the city.

sentences.zh: 奔避不及者，手擊之。

translations.literal: Those who could not flee in time he would strike with his hand.
translations.idiomatic: Those who could not flee in time he would strike with his own hand.

sentences.zh: 髡裸男女以為笑樂。

translations.literal: He shaved men and women naked for his amusement.
translations.idiomatic: He shaved men and women naked for his amusement.

sentences.zh: 十二年薨。

translations.literal: He died in the twelfth year.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twelfth year of the Yongle reign.

sentences.zh: 禮臣請追削封爵，不許。

translations.literal: The minister of rites requested that his title be posthumously stripped; the request was denied.
translations.idiomatic: The minister of rites requested that his title be posthumously stripped; the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，子簡王颙炴始得嗣。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year his son the Prince of Jian, Yong Huang, was at last allowed to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year his son the Prince of Jian, Yong Huang, was at last allowed to succeed.

sentences.zh: 縱中官擾民，洛陽人苦之。

translations.literal: He indulged eunuchs in harassing the people, and the people of Luoyang suffered greatly.
translations.idiomatic: He indulged eunuchs in harassing the people, and the people of Luoyang suffered greatly.

sentences.zh: 河南知府李驥稍持以法。

translations.literal: The prefect of Henan, Li Ji, restrained them somewhat by law.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect of Henan, Li Ji, restrained them somewhat by law.

sentences.zh: 誣奏，驥被逮治。

translations.literal: On a false accusation, Ji was arrested and tried.
translations.idiomatic: On a false accusation, Ji was arrested and tried.

sentences.zh: 己而得白，罪王左右。

translations.literal: Later the truth came out and the prince's attendants were punished.
translations.idiomatic: Later the truth came out and the prince's attendants were punished.

sentences.zh: 英宗時上表，文不恭，屢被譙讓。

translations.literal: During the Yingzong reign he submitted memorials whose wording was disrespectful and was repeatedly rebuked.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yingzong reign he submitted memorials whose wording was disrespectful and was repeatedly rebuked.

sentences.zh: 天順六年薨。

translations.literal: He died in the sixth year of Tianshun.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth year of the Tianshun reign.

sentences.zh: 世孫悼王諟釩嗣，成化十一年薨。

translations.literal: His great-grandson the Prince of Dao, Shi Fan, succeeded and died in the eleventh year of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandson the Prince of Dao, Shi Fan, succeeded and died in the eleventh year of the Chenghua reign.

sentences.zh: 弟定王諟鋝嗣，好學崇禮，居喪哀毀，歲時祀先，致齋於外。

translations.literal: His younger brother the Prince of Ding, Shi Luo, succeeded; he loved learning and honored ritual, was grief-stricken in mourning, and at the seasonal sacrifices to ancestors kept vigil fasting outside.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother the Prince of Ding, Shi Luo, succeeded him. A devoted student of the classics who honored ritual propriety, he was grief-stricken while in mourning, and at each seasonal sacrifice to his ancestors he kept vigil and fasted outside the hall.

sentences.zh: 郡王、諸將軍、中尉非慶賀不褻見。

translations.literal: County princes, various generals, and middle commandants he would not receive informally except on celebratory occasions.
translations.idiomatic: He would grant no informal audience to county princes, various generals, or middle commandants save on occasions of celebration.

sentences.zh: 民間高年者，禮下之。

translations.literal: To elderly commoners he showed respectful deference.
translations.idiomatic: To venerable elders among the common people he showed courteous deference.

sentences.zh: 正德三年薨。

translations.literal: He died in the third year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year of the Zhengde reign.

sentences.zh: 子莊王訏淵嗣，嘉靖五年薨。

translations.literal: His son the Prince of Zhuang, Xu Yuan, succeeded and died in the fifth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: His son the Prince of Zhuang, Xu Yuan, succeeded and died in the fifth year of the Jiajing reign.

sentences.zh: 弟敬王訏淳嗣，居母喪，以孝聞。

translations.literal: His younger brother the Prince of Jing, Xu Chun, succeeded; during mourning for his mother he was famed for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother the Prince of Jing, Xu Chun, succeeded. While mourning his mother he won renown for filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 以祿薄上言：「先朝以河南課鈔萬七千七百貫，準祿米八千石。

translations.literal: Because his stipend was thin he submitted a memorial: "In earlier reigns Henan tax notes totaling seventeen thousand seven hundred guan were counted as equivalent to eight thousand shi of stipend grain.
translations.idiomatic: Finding his stipend inadequate, he submitted a memorial: "In earlier reigns Henan tax notes totaling seventeen thousand seven hundred guan were reckoned equivalent to eight thousand shi of stipend grain.

sentences.zh: 八年革諸王請乞租稅，伊府課鈔亦在革中，乞補祿。」

translations.literal: In the eighth year the princes' petitions for rent and tax were abolished, and the Yi principality's tax notes were among those abolished; I beg that my stipend be restored."
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year petitions by princes for rent and tax concessions were abolished, and the Yi principality's tax notes were abolished with them. I beg that my stipend be restored."

sentences.zh: 戶部言：「課鈔本成、弘間請乞，非永樂時欽賜比。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Revenue replied: "The tax notes were originally granted upon petition during the Chenghua and Hongzhi reigns, not comparable to the imperial bestowals of the Yongle era.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Revenue replied: "Those tax notes were originally granted upon petition during the Chenghua and Hongzhi reigns—not comparable to the imperial bestowals of the Yongle era.

sentences.zh: 河南一省缺祿者八十余萬，宜不許。」

translations.literal: Henan province alone has a shortfall in stipends of more than eight hundred thousand; the request should not be granted."
translations.idiomatic: Henan province alone faces a stipend shortfall of more than eight hundred thousand; the request ought not be granted."

sentences.zh: 帝從部議。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted the ministry's recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted the ministry's recommendation.

sentences.zh: 二十一年薨。

translations.literal: He died in the twenty-first year.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twenty-first year of the Jiajing reign.

sentences.zh: 世子典楧嗣，貪而愎，多持官吏短長。

translations.literal: The heir apparent Dian Ji succeeded; he was greedy and obstinate and often seized upon officials' faults and merits.
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent Dian Ji succeeded. Greedy and stubborn, he constantly seized on officials' faults and merits to bend them to his will.

sentences.zh: 不如指，必構之去，既去復折辱之。

translations.literal: If they did not match his wishes, he inevitably framed them until they were removed; once removed he humiliated them again.
translations.idiomatic: If they failed to do as he wished, he inevitably framed them until they were driven out; and once they were gone he humiliated them afresh.

sentences.zh: 御史行部過北邙山外，典楧要笞之。

translations.literal: When a censor touring the circuit passed outside Beimang Mountain, Dian Ji intercepted and ordered him beaten.
translations.idiomatic: When a touring censor passed outside Beimang Mountain, Dian Ji waylaid him and ordered him flogged.

sentences.zh: 縉紳往來，率紆途取他境。

translations.literal: Gentry passing through generally took detours through other jurisdictions.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and gentry traveling through the region generally made long detours into neighboring jurisdictions.

sentences.zh: 經郭外者，府中人輒追挽其車，詈其不朝，入朝者復辱以非禮。

translations.literal: Those who passed outside the city walls—household staff would pursue and stop their carriages, reviling them for not paying court; those who did enter court were again insulted with impropriety.
translations.idiomatic: Those who passed outside the city walls would be pursued by household staff who seized their carriages and reviled them for failing to pay court; those who did enter were insulted again with deliberate impropriety.

sentences.zh: 府墻壞，請更築，乃奪取民舍以廣其宮。

translations.literal: When the principality walls collapsed he requested rebuilding, but instead seized commoners' dwellings to expand his palace.
translations.idiomatic: When the principality walls collapsed he petitioned to rebuild them, but instead seized commoners' houses to enlarge his palace.

sentences.zh: 郎中陳大壯與邸鄰，索其居不與，使數十人從大壯臥起，奪其飲食，竟至餒死。

translations.literal: Director Chen Dazhuang lived next to the residence; Dian Ji demanded his dwelling and when refused sent dozens of men to attend Chen day and night from waking to sleeping, seizing his food and drink, until Chen starved to death.
translations.idiomatic: Director Chen Dazhuang lived beside the princely residence. Dian Ji demanded his house; when Chen refused, he set dozens of men to attend Chen from waking to sleeping, seizing his food and drink until Chen starved to death.

sentences.zh: 所為宮，崇臺連城，擬帝闕。

translations.literal: The palace he built had lofty terraces linked to the city walls, rivaling the imperial capital.
translations.idiomatic: The palace he built rose in lofty terraces joined to the city walls, rivaling the imperial capital itself.

sentences.zh: 有錦衣官校之陜者，經洛陽，典楧忽召官屬迎詔，鼓吹擁錦衣入，捧一黃卷入宮。

translations.literal: A brocade-clad guard officer bound for Shaanxi passed through Luoyang; Dian Ji suddenly summoned his staff to receive an edict, and with music and escort the guard was brought in carrying a yellow scroll into the palace.
translations.idiomatic: A brocade-clad guard officer bound for Shaanxi passed through Luoyang. Dian Ji suddenly summoned his staff to receive an edict; with drums and pipes escorting him, the guard was ushered in bearing a yellow scroll into the palace.

sentences.zh: 眾請開讀，曰：「密詔也。」

translations.literal: The crowd asked that it be opened and read; he said: "It is a secret edict."
translations.idiomatic: The assembly asked that it be opened and read aloud. He said, "It is a secret edict."

sentences.zh: 遂趣錦衣去。

translations.literal: Then he hurried the guard away.
translations.idiomatic: Then he hurried the guard away.

sentences.zh: 錦衣謂王厚待之，不知所以。

translations.literal: The guard thought the prince had treated him with great favor and did not know why.
translations.idiomatic: The guard took this as extraordinary favor from the prince and could not fathom its meaning.

sentences.zh: 其夜大張樂，至曙，府中皆呼千歲，詐謂「天子特親我也」。

translations.literal: That night he held grand music until dawn; throughout the principality all cried "Long live!" He falsely claimed "The Son of Heaven has singled me out for special favor."
translations.idiomatic: That night he staged grand music until dawn, and throughout the principality voices cried "Long live ten thousand years!" He falsely declared, "The Son of Heaven has singled me out for special favor."

sentences.zh: 閉河南府城，大選民間子女七百余，留其姝麗者九十人。

translations.literal: He closed the Henan prefectural city and conducted a great selection of more than seven hundred youths from among the people, keeping ninety of the most beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: He shut the Henan prefectural city and conducted a great levy of more than seven hundred youths from among the people, keeping ninety of the fairest.

sentences.zh: 不中選者，令以金贖。

translations.literal: Those not selected were ordered to redeem themselves with gold.
translations.idiomatic: Those not chosen were ordered to buy their release with gold.

sentences.zh: 都御史張永明、御史林潤、給事中丘嶽相繼言其罪狀。

translations.literal: Censor-in-chief Zhang Yongming, censor Lin Run, and supervising secretary Qiu Yue successively reported his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Zhang Yongming, censor Lin Run, and supervising secretary Qiu Yue successively memorialized detailing his crimes.

sentences.zh: 再遣使往勘，革祿三之二，令壞所僭造宮城，歸民間女，執群小付有司。

translations.literal: Edicts were sent again to investigate; two-thirds of his stipend was cut; he was ordered to demolish the usurped palace and walls, return the commoners' daughters, and hand over his low associates to the authorities.
translations.idiomatic: Investigators were dispatched again. Two-thirds of his stipend was cut; he was ordered to demolish the unlawfully built palace and walls, return the commoners' daughters, and deliver his low companions to the proper authorities.

sentences.zh: 典楧不奉詔。

translations.literal: Dian Ji did not obey the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Dian Ji refused to obey the edict.

sentences.zh: 部牒促之，布政使持牒入見。

translations.literal: A ministry dispatch urged compliance; the provincial commissioner brought the dispatch in to see him.
translations.idiomatic: A ministry dispatch pressed him to comply; the provincial commissioner entered bearing the dispatch to see him.

sentences.zh: 典楧曰：「牒何為者，可用障欞耳！」

translations.literal: Dian Ji said: "What use is a dispatch? It can serve to block the window lattice!"
translations.idiomatic: Dian Ji said, "What is a dispatch good for? It can block a window lattice!"

sentences.zh: 四十三年二月，撫按官以聞。

translations.literal: In the second month of the forty-third year the provincial governor and censor reported this.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the forty-third year of the Jiajing reign, the provincial governor and censor reported this to the throne.

sentences.zh: 詔禮部會三法司議。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Ministry of Rites to convene with the three judicial offices for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the Ministry of Rites to convene the three judicial offices for joint deliberation.

sentences.zh: 僉謂：「典楧淫暴，無藩臣禮，陛下曲赦再四，終不湔改，奸回日甚。

translations.literal: All agreed: "Dian Ji is lewd and violent, without the decorum of a feudatory prince; Your Majesty has repeatedly shown merciful pardon, yet he has never reformed; his treacherous conduct grows daily.
translations.idiomatic: All agreed: "Dian Ji is lewd and violent, devoid of a feudatory prince's propriety. Your Majesty has repeatedly shown him mercy, yet he has never reformed; his treachery grows worse by the day.

sentences.zh: 宜如徽王載埨故事，禁錮高墻，削除世封。」

translations.literal: He should be treated according to the precedent of Prince Hui Zai Lun—confined within high walls and stripped of hereditary enfeoffment."
translations.idiomatic: He should be dealt with as Prince Hui Zai Lun was—confined within high walls and stripped of hereditary enfeoffment."

sentences.zh: 詔從其議，與子褒㸅俱安置開封。

translations.literal: The edict accepted their recommendation; he and his son Bao Jie were both resettled at Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: An edict accepted their recommendation. He and his son Bao Jie were both resettled at Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 皇子楠，太祖第二十六子。

translations.literal: Prince Nan, the twenty-sixth son of the Taizu Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Nan was the twenty-sixth son of the Taizu Emperor.

sentences.zh: 洪武二十六年生，逾月殤。

translations.literal: Born in the twenty-sixth year of Hongwu, he died within a month.
translations.idiomatic: Born in the twenty-sixth year of the Hongwu reign, he died before he was a month old.

sentences.zh: 靖江王守謙，太祖從孫。

translations.literal: Prince Jingjiang Shouqian was a grand-nephew of the Taizu Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jingjiang Shouqian was a grand-nephew of the Taizu Emperor.

sentences.zh: 父文正，南昌王子也。

translations.literal: His father Wenzheng was a son of the Prince of Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wenzheng was a son of the Prince of Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 當太祖起兵時，南昌王前死，妻王氏攜文正依太祖。

translations.literal: When the Taizu Emperor raised his army, the Prince of Nanchang had already died; his wife Lady Wang brought Wenzheng to rely on the Taizu Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: When the Taizu Emperor first raised his army, the Prince of Nanchang was already dead; his widow Lady Wang brought Wenzheng to live under the Taizu Emperor's protection.

sentences.zh: 太祖、高後撫如己子。

translations.literal: The Taizu Emperor and the Empress Gao nurtured them as their own children.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu Emperor and Empress Gao reared them as though they were their own children.

sentences.zh: 比長，涉獵傳記，饒勇略，隨渡江取集慶路。

translations.literal: When he grew up he ranged through histories and annals, possessed abundant courage and stratagem, and crossed the Yangzi with the army to take Jiqing Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age he read widely in histories and chronicles, showed abundant courage and strategic talent, and crossed the Yangzi with the army to take Jiqing Circuit.

sentences.zh: 已，有功，授樞密院同僉。

translations.literal: Soon, for merit, he was appointed vice commissioner of the Privy Council.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, for his achievements, he was appointed vice commissioner of the Privy Council.

sentences.zh: 太祖從容問：「若欲何官？」

translations.literal: The Taizu Emperor asked him at ease: "What office would you like?"
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu Emperor asked him casually, "What office would you like?"

sentences.zh: 文正對曰：「叔父成大業，何患不富貴。

translations.literal: Wenzheng replied: "When my uncle completes the great enterprise, why worry about not being rich and noble?
translations.idiomatic: Wenzheng answered, "Once my uncle completes the great enterprise, why should I worry over wealth and rank?

sentences.zh: 爵賞先私親，何以服眾！」

translations.literal: If titles and rewards go first to private kin, how can the multitude be satisfied!"
translations.idiomatic: If titles and rewards go first to one's own kin, how will the multitude be won over!"

sentences.zh: 太祖喜其言，益愛之。

translations.literal: The Taizu Emperor was pleased with his words and loved him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu Emperor was pleased with this answer and cherished him all the more.

sentences.zh: 太祖為吳王，命為大都督，節制中外諸軍事。

translations.literal: When the Taizu Emperor became King of Wu, he appointed Wenzheng grand councillor of war, directing all military affairs within and without.
translations.idiomatic: When the Taizu Emperor became King of Wu, he appointed Wenzheng grand councillor of war with authority over all military affairs at home and abroad.

sentences.zh: 及再定江西，以洪都重鎮，屏翰西南，非骨肉重臣莫能守。

translations.literal: When Jiangxi was pacified again, as Hongdu was a vital stronghold, the bulwark of the southwest, none but a close kinsman and weighty minister could hold it.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangxi was pacified anew, Hongdu stood as a vital stronghold—the shield of the southwest—and none but a close kinsman and trusted minister could hold it.

sentences.zh: 乃命文正統元帥趙得勝等鎮其地，儒士郭之章、劉仲服為參謀。

translations.literal: He therefore ordered Wenzheng to command the area with marshals such as Zhao Desheng, and appointed the scholars Guo Zhizhang and Liu Zhong as strategists.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore put Wenzheng in command of the region with marshals such as Zhao Desheng, and appointed the scholars Guo Zhizhang and Liu Zhong as his strategists.

sentences.zh: 文正增城浚池，招集山寨未附者，號令明肅，遠近震懾。

translations.literal: Wenzheng enlarged the walls and deepened the moat, gathered in those from mountain strongholds who had not yet submitted, and his orders were clear and stern; near and far were awed.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzheng raised the walls and dredged the moat, drew in those in mountain strongholds who had not yet submitted, and issued orders so clear and stern that the region near and far trembled before him.

sentences.zh: 居無何，友諒帥舟師六十萬圍洪都。

translations.literal: Before long, Youliang led six hundred thousand men in ships to besiege Hongdu.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Chen Youliang led six hundred thousand men in ships to besiege Hongdu.

sentences.zh: 文正數摧其鋒，堅守八十有五日，城壞復完者數十丈。

translations.literal: Wenzheng repeatedly broke their momentum and held firm for eighty-five days; where the walls were breached they were rebuilt for dozens of zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzheng repeatedly shattered their assault and held firm for eighty-five days; wherever the walls were breached, tens of zhang were rebuilt overnight.

sentences.zh: 友諒旁掠吉安、臨江，俘其守將徇城下，不為動。

translations.literal: Youliang raided Ji'an and Linjiang on the side and paraded their captured garrison commanders beneath the walls, but Wenzheng was unmoved.
translations.idiomatic: Youliang raided Ji'an and Linjiang on the flank and paraded captured garrison commanders beneath the walls, yet Wenzheng did not waver.

sentences.zh: 太祖親帥兵來援，友諒乃解去，與太祖相拒於彭蠡。

translations.literal: The Taizu Emperor personally led troops to the relief; Youliang then lifted the siege and faced off against the Taizu Emperor at Poyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu Emperor personally led an army to relieve the city; Youliang then withdrew and confronted him at Lake Poyang.

sentences.zh: 友諒掠糧都昌，文正遣方亮焚其舟。

translations.literal: Youliang foraged for grain at Duchang; Wenzheng sent Fang Liang to burn his ships.
translations.idiomatic: Youliang foraged for grain at Duchang; Wenzheng sent Fang Liang to burn his fleet.

sentences.zh: 糧道絕，友諒遂敗。

translations.literal: The grain route was cut off and Youliang was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: With his supply line severed, Youliang was defeated.

sentences.zh: 復遣何文輝等討平未附州縣。

translations.literal: Wenzheng again sent He Wenhui and others to pacify unsubmitted prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzheng again dispatched He Wenhui and others to subdue prefectures and counties that had not yet submitted.

sentences.zh: 江西之平，文正功居多。

translations.literal: In the pacification of Jiangxi, Wenzheng's merit was foremost.
translations.idiomatic: In the pacification of Jiangxi, Wenzheng's merit stood foremost.

sentences.zh: 太祖還京，告廟飲至，賜常遇春、廖永忠及諸將士金帛甚厚。

translations.literal: The Taizu Emperor returned to the capital, offered report at the ancestral temple, and held a victory feast, bestowing gold and silk very generously on Chang Yuchun, Liao Yongzhong, and the other officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu Emperor returned to the capital, reported victory at the ancestral temple, and held a feast of triumph, lavishing gold and silk on Chang Yuchun, Liao Yongzhong, and the other commanders and soldiers.

sentences.zh: 念文正前言知大體，錫功尚有待也，而文正不能無少望。

translations.literal: Remembering Wenzheng's earlier words showing grasp of the larger principle, reward for merit was still pending; yet Wenzheng could not be without some disappointment.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful of Wenzheng's earlier words, which showed he understood the larger principle, the Taizu Emperor still held his reward in abeyance; yet Wenzheng could not altogether suppress his disappointment.

sentences.zh: 性素卡急，至是暴怒，遂失常度，任掾吏衛可達奪部中子女。

translations.literal: By nature he had always been stern and irritable; now in violent rage he lost all measure and allowed his clerk Wei Keda to seize men and women from among his subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he had always been impatient and severe; now, in a fit of rage, he lost all restraint and let his clerk Wei Keda seize men and women from among his subordinates.

sentences.zh: 按察使李飲冰奏其驕侈觖望，太祖遣使詰責。

translations.literal: Surveillance commissioner Li Yinbing memorialized about his arrogance, extravagance, and discontent; the Taizu Emperor sent emissaries to rebuke him.
translations.idiomatic: Surveillance commissioner Li Yinbing memorialized accusing him of arrogance, extravagance, and disaffection; the Taizu Emperor sent envoys to rebuke him.

sentences.zh: 文正懼，飲冰益言其有異志。

translations.literal: Wenzheng was afraid, and Yinbing further reported that he harbored rebellious intent.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzheng was frightened, and Yinbing further reported that he harbored rebellious intent.

sentences.zh: 太祖即日登舟至城下，遣人召之。

translations.literal: That very day the Taizu Emperor boarded a boat and came to beneath the city walls, sending men to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: That very day the Taizu Emperor boarded a boat and came beneath the city walls, sending men to summon him.

sentences.zh: 文天上倉卒出迎，太祖數曰：「汝何為者？」

translations.literal: Wenzheng came out in haste to meet him; the Taizu Emperor berated him: "What do you think you are doing?"
translations.idiomatic: Wenzheng rushed out to meet him. The Taizu Emperor upbraided him: "What do you think you are doing?"

sentences.zh: 遂載與俱歸，欲竟其事。

translations.literal: He then took him aboard and returned together, intending to settle the matter completely.
translations.idiomatic: He then took Wenzheng aboard and returned with him, intending to see the matter through to the end.

sentences.zh: 高後力解之曰：「兒特性剛耳，無他也。」

translations.literal: The Empress Gao vigorously interceded, saying: "The boy is simply stubborn by nature; there is nothing else."
translations.idiomatic: Empress Gao interceded forcefully, saying, "The boy is simply stubborn by nature—there is nothing more to it."

sentences.zh: 免官安置桐城，未幾卒。

translations.literal: He was dismissed from office and resettled at Tongcheng; before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzheng was stripped of office and resettled at Tongcheng; before long he died.

sentences.zh: 飲冰亦以他事伏誅。

translations.literal: Yinbing was also executed on other charges.
translations.idiomatic: Yinbing was also executed on other charges.

sentences.zh: 文正之被謫也，守謙甫四歲，太祖撫其頂曰：「兒無恐，爾父倍訓教，貽我憂，我終不以爾父故廢爾。」

translations.literal: When Wenzheng was banished, Shouqian was only four years old; the Taizu Emperor stroked his head and said: "Child, do not fear. Your father has disobeyed instruction and instruction, causing me worry, but I will never discard you because of your father."
translations.idiomatic: When Wenzheng was banished, Shouqian was only four. The Taizu Emperor stroked his head and said, "Child, do not be afraid. Your father has turned against all instruction and brought me grief, yet I will never cast you aside because of your father."

sentences.zh: 育之宮中。

translations.literal: He raised him in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: He reared him in the palace.

sentences.zh: 守謙幼名鐵柱，吳元年以諸子命名告廟，更名煒。

translations.literal: Shouqian's childhood name was Tiezhu; in the first year of Wu, when the sons were given names and reported to the temple, he was renamed Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Shouqian's childhood name was Tiezhu. In the first year of Wu, when the sons were given formal names and the rite was reported at the ancestral temple, he was renamed Wei.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年更名守謙，封靖江王。

translations.literal: In the third year of Hongwu he was renamed Shouqian and enfeoffed as Prince of Jingjiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Hongwu reign he was renamed Shouqian and enfeoffed as Prince of Jingjiang.

sentences.zh: 祿視郡王，官屬親王之半，命耆儒趙壎為長史傅之。

translations.literal: His stipend was on the scale of a commandery prince; his staff was half that of a full prince; the aged scholar Zhao Xun was appointed chief administrator to tutor him.
translations.idiomatic: His stipend matched that of a commandery prince, his staff half that of a full prince; the venerable scholar Zhao Xun was appointed chief administrator to instruct him.

sentences.zh: 既長，之藩桂林。

translations.literal: When he came of age he went to his fief at Guilin.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age he went to take up his fief at Guilin.

sentences.zh: 桂林有元順帝潛邸，改為王宮，上表謝。

translations.literal: Guilin had the Yuan Emperor Shundi's former covert residence, which was converted into his princely palace; he submitted a memorial of thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Guilin held the Yuan Emperor Shundi's former hidden residence, which was converted into his princely palace; he submitted a memorial of thanks.

sentences.zh: 太祖敕其從臣曰：「從孫幼而遠鎮西南，其善導之。」

translations.literal: The Taizu Emperor instructed his attending ministers: "My grand-nephew is young and holds a distant post in the southwest; guide him well."
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu Emperor instructed his attendants: "My grand-nephew is young and holds a distant post in the southwest; guide him well."

sentences.zh: 守謙知書，而好比群小，粵人怨咨。

translations.literal: Shouqian was literate but loved to consort with low companions; the people of Yue complained bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: Shouqian was learned, yet he delighted in low companions; the people of Yue groaned under his rule.

sentences.zh: 召還，戒諭之。

translations.literal: He was recalled and admonished.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to court and admonished.

sentences.zh: 守謙作詩怨望。

translations.literal: Shouqian composed poetry expressing resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Shouqian wrote poems full of resentment.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，廢為庶人。

translations.literal: The emperor was angered and demoted him to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged and reduced him to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 居鳳陽七年，復其爵。

translations.literal: After seven years at Fengyang his title was restored.
translations.idiomatic: After seven years at Fengyang his title was restored.

sentences.zh: 徙鎮雲南，使其妃弟徐溥同往，賜書戒飭，語極摯切。

translations.literal: He was transferred to hold Yunnan; his consort's younger brother Xu Pu was sent with him; an imperial letter of admonition was bestowed, its words extremely earnest.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to hold Yunnan; his consort's younger brother Xu Pu was sent with him, and an imperial letter of stern admonition was bestowed, its words deeply earnest.

sentences.zh: 守謙暴橫如故。

translations.literal: Shouqian was violent and overbearing as before.
translations.idiomatic: Shouqian was violent and overbearing as before.

sentences.zh: 召還，使再居鳳陽。

translations.literal: He was recalled and made to live at Fengyang again.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled and sent to live at Fengyang again.

sentences.zh: 復以強取牧馬，錮之京師。

translations.literal: Again, for forcibly seizing pasturing horses, he was confined in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Again, for forcibly seizing pasturing horses, he was confined in the capital.

sentences.zh: 二十五年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the twenty-fifth year.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twenty-fifth year of the Hongwu reign.

sentences.zh: 子贊儀幼，命為世子。

translations.literal: His son Zanyi was young and was appointed heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zanyi was still young and was appointed heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 三十年春遣省晉、燕、周、楚、齊、蜀、湘、代、肅、遼、慶、谷、秦十三王，自湘、楚入蜀，歷陜西，抵河南、山西、北平，東至大寧、遼陽，還自山東，使知親親之義，熟山川險易，習勞苦。贊儀恭慎好學。永樂元年復之國桂林，使蕭用道為長史。用道善輔導，贊儀亦敬禮之。六年薨，謚曰悼僖。

translations.literal: In the spring of year thirty, he was sent to visit the thirteen princes of Jin, Yan, Zhou, Chu, Qi, Shu, Xiang, Dai, Su, Liao, Qing, Gu, and Qin. From Xiang and Chu he entered Shu, passed through Shaanxi, reached Henan, Shanxi, and Beiping, went east to Daning and Liaoyang, and returned by way of Shandong, so that he would know the meaning of affection among kin, become familiar with the difficulty and ease of mountains and rivers, and become accustomed to hardship. Zanyi was respectful, cautious, and fond of learning. In Yongle year one he again went to his state at Guilin, and Xiao Yongdao was made his chief secretary. Yongdao was good at guiding and assisting him, and Zanyi also honored him with respect and ritual. He died in year six and was posthumously titled Daoxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Hongwu 30, Zanyi was sent to visit the thirteen princes of Jin, Yan, Zhou, Chu, Qi, Shu, Xiang, Dai, Su, Liao, Qing, Gu, and Qin. From Xiang and Chu he entered Shu, passed through Shaanxi, reached Henan, Shanxi, and Beiping, went east to Daning and Liaoyang, and returned through Shandong. The purpose was to teach him the duty of affection among kin, make him familiar with the strengths and weaknesses of the terrain, and accustom him to hardship. Zanyi was respectful, cautious, and fond of learning. In Yongle 1 he again went to his state at Guilin, with Xiao Yongdao appointed as his chief secretary. Xiao was skilled at guidance, and Zanyi treated him with honor and respect. Zanyi died in Yongle 6 and received the posthumous title Daoxi.

sentences.zh: 子莊簡王佐敬嗣。

translations.literal: His son the Prince of Zhuangjian, Zuo Jing, succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son the Prince of Zhuangjian, Zuo Jing, succeeded.

sentences.zh: 初給銀印，宣德中，改用金塗。

translations.literal: At first he was given a silver seal; during Xuande it was changed to gold-plated.
translations.idiomatic: At first he was granted a silver seal; during the Xuande reign it was changed to gold-plated.

sentences.zh: 正統初，與其弟奉國將軍佐敏相訐奏，語連大學士楊榮。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengtong he and his younger brother the State-Supporting General Zuo Min exchanged accusatory memorials, their words implicating Grand Secretary Yang Rong.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhengtong reign he and his younger brother, the State-Supporting General Zuo Min, exchanged accusatory memorials that implicated Grand Secretary Yang Rong.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，戍其使人。

translations.literal: The emperor was angered and banished their envoys to frontier service.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angered and banished their messengers to frontier service.

sentences.zh: 成化五年薨。

translations.literal: He died in the fifth year of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth year of the Chenghua reign.

sentences.zh: 子相承先卒，孫昭和王規裕嗣，弘治二年薨。

translations.literal: His son Chengxian died first; his grandson the Prince of Zhaohe, Gui Yu, succeeded and died in the second year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chengxian had died earlier; his grandson the Prince of Zhaohe, Gui Yu, succeeded and died in the second year of the Hongzhi reign.

sentences.zh: 子端懿王約麒嗣，以孝謹聞。

translations.literal: His son the Prince of Duanyi, Yue Qi, succeeded and was known for filial piety and prudence.
translations.idiomatic: His son the Prince of Duanyi, Yue Qi, succeeded and was known for filial piety and sober conduct.

sentences.zh: 正德十一年薨。

translations.literal: He died in the eleventh year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eleventh year of the Zhengde reign.

sentences.zh: 子安肅王經扶嗣，好學有儉德，嘗為《敬義箴》。

translations.literal: His son the Prince of Ansu, Jing Fu, succeeded; he loved learning and had a frugal virtue; he once wrote "Admonition on Reverence and Righteousness."
translations.idiomatic: His son the Prince of Ansu, Jing Fu, succeeded. He loved learning and practiced thrift; he once composed the "Admonition on Reverence and Righteousness."

sentences.zh: 嘉靖四年薨。

translations.literal: He died in the fourth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of the Jiajing reign.

sentences.zh: 子恭惠王邦苧嗣，與巡按御史徐南金相訐奏。

translations.literal: His son the Prince of Gonghui, Bang Ning, succeeded; he and the touring censor Xu Nanjin exchanged accusatory memorials.
translations.idiomatic: His son the Prince of Gonghui, Bang Ning, succeeded. He and the touring censor Xu Nanjin exchanged accusatory memorials against each other.

sentences.zh: 奪祿米，罪其官校。

translations.literal: Stipend grain was stripped away and his staff officers were punished.
translations.idiomatic: The court stripped his stipend grain and punished his staff officers.

sentences.zh: 隆慶六年薨。

translations.literal: He died in the sixth year of Longqing.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth year of the Longqing reign.

sentences.zh: 子康僖王任昌嗣，萬歷十年薨。

translations.literal: His son the Prince of Kangxi, Ren Chang, succeeded and died in the tenth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: His son the Prince of Kangxi, Ren Chang, succeeded and died in the tenth year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 子溫裕王履燾嗣，二十年薨。

translations.literal: His son the Prince of Wenyu, Lü Zhan, succeeded and died in the twentieth year.
translations.idiomatic: His son the Prince of Wenyu, Lü Zhan, succeeded and died in the twentieth year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 無子，從父憲定王任晟嗣，三十八年薨。

translations.literal: Having no son, his cousin the Prince of Xianding, Ren Sheng, succeeded from the father's line and died in the thirty-eighth year.
translations.idiomatic: Having no son, he was succeeded by his cousin the Prince of Xianding, Ren Sheng; he died in the thirty-eighth year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 子榮穆王履祜嗣，薨。

translations.literal: His son the Prince of Rongmu, Lü Hu, succeeded and died.
translations.idiomatic: His son the Prince of Rongmu, Lü Hu, succeeded and died.

sentences.zh: 子亨嘉嗣。

translations.literal: His son Heng Jia succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Heng Jia succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 李自成陷京師後，自稱監國於廣西，為巡撫瞿式耜所誅。

translations.literal: After Li Zicheng captured the capital, he styled himself regent in Guangxi and was executed by the governor-general Qu Shisi.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Zicheng captured the capital, he proclaimed himself regent in Guangxi and was put to death by the governor-general Qu Shisi.

sentences.zh: 時唐王聿鍵在福建，奏捷焉。

translations.literal: At the time the Prince of Tang, Yujian, was in Fujian and reported the victory.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Prince of Tang, Yujian, was in Fujian and reported the victory there.

sentences.zh: 興宗五子。

translations.literal: Xingzong had five sons.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xingzong had five sons.

sentences.zh: 後常氏生虞懷王雄英、吳王允熥。

translations.literal: Later Lady Chang bore the Prince of Yuhuai, Xiong Ying, and the Prince of Wu, Yun Bing.
translations.idiomatic: Later Lady Chang bore the Prince of Yuhuai, Xiong Ying, and the Prince of Wu, Yun Bing.

sentences.zh: 呂後生惠帝、衡王允熞、徐王允𤐤。

translations.literal: Empress Lü bore the Emperor of Hui, the Prince of Heng, Yun Yan, and the Prince of Xu, Yun Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Lü bore the Emperor of Hui, the Prince of Heng, Yun Yan, and the Prince of Xu, Yun Xian.

sentences.zh: 虞懷王雄英，興宗長子，太祖嫡長孫也。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yuhuai, Xiong Ying, was Xingzong's eldest son and the Taizu's eldest grandson by the principal consort.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yuhuai, Xiong Ying, was Prince Xingzong's eldest son and the Taizu Emperor's eldest grandson by the principal consort.

sentences.zh: 洪武十五年五月薨。

translations.literal: He died in the fifth month of the fifteenth year of Hongwu.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth month of the fifteenth year of the Hongwu reign.

sentences.zh: 年八歲。

translations.literal: He was eight years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was eight years old.

sentences.zh: 追加封謚。

translations.literal: Posthumous title and enfeoffment were added.
translations.idiomatic: A posthumous title and enfeoffment were conferred upon him.

sentences.zh: 吳王允熥，興宗第三子。

translations.literal: The Prince of Wu, Yun Bing, was Xingzong's third son.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Wu, Yun Bing, was Prince Xingzong's third son.

sentences.zh: 建文元年封國杭州，未之藩。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianwen he was enfeoffed at Hangzhou but did not proceed to his fief.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Jianwen reign he was enfeoffed at Hangzhou but never proceeded to his fief.

sentences.zh: 成祖即位，降為廣澤王，居漳州。

translations.literal: When the Yongle Emperor took the throne, he was demoted to Prince of Guangze and dwelt at Zhangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yongle Emperor took the throne, he was demoted to Prince of Guangze and sent to live at Zhangzhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，召還京，廢為庶人，錮鳳陽。

translations.literal: Before long he was summoned back to the capital, stripped of rank and made a commoner, and confined at Fengyang.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was summoned back to the capital, reduced to commoner status, and confined at Fengyang.

sentences.zh: 永樂十五年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the fifteenth year of Yongle.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifteenth year of the Yongle reign.

sentences.zh: 衡王允熞，興宗第四子，建文元年封。

translations.literal: The Prince of Heng, Yun Yan, was Xingzong's fourth son and was enfeoffed in the first year of Jianwen.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Heng, Yun Yan, was Prince Xingzong's fourth son and was enfeoffed in the first year of the Jianwen reign.

sentences.zh: 成祖降為懷恩王，居建昌。

translations.literal: The Yongle Emperor demoted him to Prince of Huai'en and sent him to live at Jianchang.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongle Emperor demoted him to Prince of Huai'en and sent him to live at Jianchang.

sentences.zh: 與允熥俱召還，錮鳳陽，先後卒。

translations.literal: He and Yun Bing were both summoned back and confined at Fengyang, dying one after the other.
translations.idiomatic: He and Yun Bing were both summoned back and confined at Fengyang, where they died in succession.

sentences.zh: 徐王允𤐤，興宗第五子，建文元年封。

translations.literal: The Prince of Xu, Yun Xian, was Xingzong's fifth son and was enfeoffed in the first year of Jianwen.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Xu, Yun Xian, was Prince Xingzong's fifth son and was enfeoffed in the first year of the Jianwen reign.

sentences.zh: 成祖降為敷惠王，隨母呂太后居懿文陵。

translations.literal: The Yongle Emperor demoted him to Prince of Fuhui; he dwelt with his mother Empress Dowager Lü at the Yiwen Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongle Emperor demoted him to Prince of Fuhui, and he lived with his mother, Empress Dowager Lü, at the Yiwen Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 永樂二年下詔改甌寧王，奉太子祀。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongle an edict renamed him Prince of Ouning and charged him with maintaining rites for the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Yongle reign an edict renamed him Prince of Ouning and charged him with maintaining rites for the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 四年十二月，邸中火，暴薨。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the fourth year fire broke out in his residence and he died suddenly.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the fourth year a fire broke out in his residence and he died suddenly.

sentences.zh: 謚曰哀簡。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Ai Jian.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously titled Ai Jian.

sentences.zh: 惠帝二子。俱馬後生。太子文奎。建文元年立為皇太子。燕師入，七歲矣，莫知所終。

translations.literal: Emperor Hui had two sons. Both were born to Empress Ma. The crown prince was Wenkui. In Jianwen year one he was established as crown prince. When the Yan army entered, he was seven years old, and no one knew where he ended.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Hui had two sons, both born to Empress Ma. The crown prince was Wenkui, who was made heir apparent in Jianwen 1. When the Yan army entered the capital he was seven years old, and no one knew what became of him.

sentences.zh: 少子文圭。

translations.literal: His youngest son was Wen Gui.
translations.idiomatic: He left a youngest son, Wen Gui.

sentences.zh: 年二歲，成祖入，幽之中都廣安宮，號為建庶人。

translations.literal: At the age of two, when the Yongle Emperor entered the capital, he was confined in the Guang'an Palace at the central capital and styled the Jian Commoner.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of two, when the Yongle Emperor entered the capital, he was confined in the Guang'an Palace at the secondary capital and styled the Jian Commoner.

sentences.zh: 英宗復辟，憐庶人無罪久系，欲釋之，左右或以為不可。

translations.literal: When the Yingzong Emperor restored the throne, he pitied the commoner's long imprisonment without crime and wished to release him, but those around him thought it inadvisable.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yingzong Emperor restored the throne, he pitied the commoner's long imprisonment without crime and wished to release him, but his advisors thought it inadvisable.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「有天命者，任自為之。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "He whom Heaven favors may do as he will."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "He whom Heaven favors may do as he will."

sentences.zh: 大學士李賢贊曰：「此堯、舜之心也。」

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Li Xian applauded: "This is the heart of Yao and Shun."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Li Xian applauded, "This is the heart of Yao and Shun."

sentences.zh: 遂請於太后，命內臣牛玉往出之。

translations.literal: He then asked the empress dowager and ordered the eunuch Niu Yu to go and release him.
translations.idiomatic: He then petitioned the empress dowager and ordered the eunuch Niu Yu to go and release him.

sentences.zh: 聽居鳳陽，婚娶出入使自便。

translations.literal: He was permitted to live at Fengyang, with freedom to marry and come and go as he pleased.
translations.idiomatic: He was permitted to live at Fengyang, with freedom to marry and come and go as he pleased.

sentences.zh: 與閽者二十人，婢妾十余人，給使令。

translations.literal: He was given twenty gatekeepers and more than ten maids and concubines to serve him.
translations.idiomatic: He was given twenty gatekeepers and more than ten maids and concubines to attend him.

sentences.zh: 文圭孩提被幽，至是年五十七矣。

translations.literal: Wen Gui had been confined since infancy; by now he was fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Gui had been confined since infancy; by now he was fifty-seven years old.

sentences.zh: 未幾卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died.

sentences.zh: 成祖四子。

translations.literal: The Yongle Emperor had four sons.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongle Emperor had four sons.

sentences.zh: 仁宗、漢王高煦、趙王高燧俱文皇后生。

translations.literal: The Renzong Emperor, the Prince of Han, Gao Xu, and the Prince of Zhao, Gao Sui, were all born to Empress Wen.
translations.idiomatic: The Renzong Emperor, the Prince of Han, Gao Xu, and the Prince of Zhao, Gao Sui, were all born to Empress Wen.

sentences.zh: 高爔未詳所生母。

translations.literal: Gao Xi's birth mother is not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xi's birth mother is not recorded.

sentences.zh: 漢王高煦，成祖第二子。

translations.literal: The Prince of Han, Gao Xu, was the Yongle Emperor's second son.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Han, Gao Xu, was the Yongle Emperor's second son.

sentences.zh: 性兇悍。

translations.literal: By nature he was fierce and overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was fierce and overbearing.

sentences.zh: 洪武時，召諸王子學於京師。

translations.literal: During the Hongwu reign, the princes' sons were summoned to study in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: During the Hongwu reign, the sons of the princes were summoned to study in the capital.

sentences.zh: 高煦不肯學，言動輕佻，為太祖所惡。

translations.literal: Gao Xu refused to study; his words and conduct were frivolous, and the Taizu detested him.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xu refused to study. His words and conduct were frivolous, and the Taizu Emperor detested him.

sentences.zh: 及太祖崩，成祖遣仁宗及高煦入臨京師。

translations.literal: When the Taizu died, the Yongle Emperor sent the Renzong and Gao Xu to attend the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the Taizu Emperor died, the Yongle Emperor sent the Renzong and Gao Xu to attend the capital.

sentences.zh: 舅徐輝祖以其無賴，密戒之。

translations.literal: His uncle Xu Huizu, finding him unruly, secretly warned him.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Xu Huizu, finding him unruly, secretly admonished him.

sentences.zh: 不聽，盜輝祖善馬，徑渡江馳歸。

translations.literal: He would not listen, stole Xu Huizu's fine horse, crossed the river directly and galloped home.
translations.idiomatic: He would not listen. He stole Xu Huizu's finest horse, crossed the river, and galloped straight home.

sentences.zh: 途中輒殺民吏，至涿州，又擊殺驛丞，於是朝臣舉以責燕。

translations.literal: Along the way he killed commoners and officials; at Zhuozhou he also struck dead the post-station director, whereupon court officials cited this to rebuke the Prince of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Along the way he killed commoners and officials. At Zhuozhou he also struck dead the post-station director, whereupon court officials cited these crimes to rebuke the Prince of Yan.

sentences.zh: 成祖起兵，仁宗居守，高煦從，嘗為軍鋒。

translations.literal: When the Yongle Emperor raised troops, the Renzong remained to hold the base while Gao Xu followed and sometimes served as the army's vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yongle Emperor raised troops, the Renzong remained behind to hold the base while Gao Xu followed him and sometimes served as the army's vanguard.

sentences.zh: 白溝河之戰，成祖幾為瞿能所及，高煦帥精騎數千，直前決戰，斬能父子於陣。

translations.literal: At the Battle of Baigou River the Yongle Emperor was nearly caught by Qu Neng; Gao Xu led several thousand elite cavalry straight forward to decide the battle and killed Qu Neng and his son in the fray.
translations.idiomatic: At the Battle of Baigou River the Yongle Emperor was nearly caught by Qu Neng. Gao Xu led several thousand elite cavalry straight into the deciding fight and killed Qu Neng and his son on the field.

sentences.zh: 及成祖東昌之敗，張玉戰死，成祖只身走，適高煦引師至，擊退南軍。

translations.literal: When the Yongle Emperor was defeated at Dongchang and Zhang Yu died in battle, the emperor fled alone; just then Gao Xu arrived with his forces and drove back the southern army.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yongle Emperor was defeated at Dongchang and Zhang Yu died in battle, the emperor fled alone. Just then Gao Xu arrived with his forces and drove back the southern army.

sentences.zh: 徐輝祖敗燕兵於浦子口，高煦引蕃騎來。

translations.literal: Xu Huizu defeated the Yan forces at Puzikou; Gao Xu brought barbarian cavalry to the field.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Huizu defeated the Yan forces at Puzikou, and Gao Xu brought barbarian cavalry to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 成祖大喜，曰：「吾力疲矣，兒當鼓勇再戰。」

translations.literal: The Yongle Emperor was greatly pleased and said: "I am exhausted; my son must rouse his courage and fight again."
translations.idiomatic: The Yongle Emperor was greatly pleased and said, "I am exhausted. My son must rouse his courage and fight again."

sentences.zh: 高煦麾蕃騎力戰，南軍遂卻。

translations.literal: Gao Xu commanded the barbarian cavalry to fight hard, and the southern army then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xu commanded the barbarian cavalry to fight with all their strength, and the southern army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 成祖屢瀕於危而轉敗為功者，高煦力為多。

translations.literal: In the many times the Yongle Emperor barely escaped danger and turned defeat into victory, Gao Xu's exertions counted for much.
translations.idiomatic: In the many moments when the Yongle Emperor barely escaped danger and turned defeat into victory, Gao Xu's exertions counted for much.

sentences.zh: 成祖以為類己，高煦亦以此自負，恃功驕恣，多不法。

translations.literal: The Yongle Emperor thought him like himself; Gao Xu also took pride in this, relied on his merits, grew arrogant and wilful, and committed many unlawful acts.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongle Emperor thought him like himself, and Gao Xu took pride in it. Relying on his merits, he grew arrogant and wilful and committed many unlawful acts.

sentences.zh: 成祖即位，命將兵往開平備邊。

translations.literal: When the Yongle Emperor took the throne, he ordered him to command troops to garrison Kaiping and guard the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yongle Emperor took the throne, he ordered Gao Xu to command troops at Kaiping to guard the frontier.

sentences.zh: 時議建儲，淇國公丘福、駙馬王寧善高煦，時時稱高煦功高，幾奪嫡。

translations.literal: At the time the heir was being chosen; the Duke of Qi, Qiu Fu, and the imperial son-in-law Wang Ning favored Gao Xu and constantly praised his high merits, nearly displacing the eldest son from succession.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the heir was being chosen, the Duke of Qi, Qiu Fu, and the imperial son-in-law Wang Ning favored Gao Xu and constantly praised his high merits, nearly displacing the eldest son from succession.

sentences.zh: 成祖卒以元子仁賢，且太祖所立，而高煦又多過失，不果。

translations.literal: The Yongle Emperor finally chose the eldest son for his benevolence and worth, and because the Taizu had established him, while Gao Xu had many faults; it did not come to pass.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongle Emperor finally chose the eldest son for his benevolence and worth—the Taizu had established him—and because Gao Xu had many faults, the plan did not succeed.

sentences.zh: 永樂二年，仁宗立為太子，封高煦漢王，國雲南。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongle the Renzong was established as crown prince; Gao Xu was enfeoffed as Prince of Han with his fief in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Yongle reign the Renzong was established as crown prince, and Gao Xu was enfeoffed as Prince of Han with his fief in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 高煦曰：「我何罪！

translations.literal: Gao Xu said: "What is my crime!
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xu said, "What is my crime!

sentences.zh: 斥萬里。」

translations.literal: Banished ten thousand li away."
translations.idiomatic: To be banished ten thousand li away!"

sentences.zh: 不肯行。

translations.literal: He refused to go.
translations.idiomatic: He refused to go.

sentences.zh: 從成祖巡北京，力請並其子歸南京。

translations.literal: Accompanying the Yongle Emperor on his tour of Beijing, he urgently petitioned that he and his sons be allowed to return to Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Accompanying the Yongle Emperor on his tour of Beijing, he urgently petitioned to be allowed to return to Nanjing with his sons.

sentences.zh: 成祖不得已，聽之。

translations.literal: The Yongle Emperor had no choice and granted it.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongle Emperor had no choice and granted his request.

sentences.zh: 請得天策衛為護衛，輒以唐太宗自比。

translations.literal: He requested the Tiance Guard as his bodyguard and constantly compared himself to Emperor Taizong of Tang.
translations.idiomatic: He requested the Tiance Guard as his bodyguard and constantly compared himself to Emperor Taizong of Tang.

sentences.zh: 己，復乘間請益兩護衛，所為益恣。

translations.literal: Then, seizing an opportunity, he again requested two more bodyguards; his conduct grew ever more unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: Then, seizing an opportunity, he again requested two more bodyguards, and his conduct grew ever more unrestrained.

sentences.zh: 成祖嘗命同仁宗謁孝陵。

translations.literal: The Yongle Emperor once ordered him to go with the Renzong to pay respects at the Xiaoling Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongle Emperor once ordered him to go with the Renzong to pay respects at the Xiaoling Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 仁宗體肥重，且足疾，兩中使掖之行，恒失足。

translations.literal: The Renzong was stout and heavy and had a foot ailment; two eunuchs supported him as he walked, and he constantly stumbled.
translations.idiomatic: The Renzong was stout and heavy and suffered from a foot ailment. Two eunuchs supported him as he walked, and he constantly stumbled.

sentences.zh: 高煦從後言曰：「前人蹉跌，後人知警。」

translations.literal: Gao Xu spoke from behind and said: "When those ahead stumble, those behind take warning."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xu spoke from behind and said, "When those ahead stumble, those behind take warning."

sentences.zh: 時宣宗為皇太孫，在後應聲曰：「更有後人知警也。」

translations.literal: At the time the Xuande Emperor, as heir presumptive, answered from behind: "There are those behind who will take warning too."
translations.idiomatic: At the time the future Xuande Emperor, as heir presumptive, answered from behind, "There are those behind who will take warning too."

sentences.zh: 高煦回顧失色。

translations.literal: Gao Xu looked back and changed color.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xu looked back and blanched.

sentences.zh: 高煦長七尺余，輕趫善騎射，兩腋若龍鱗者數片。

translations.literal: Gao Xu was more than seven chi tall, light and nimble, skilled at horsemanship and archery, with several scales like dragon scales under both armpits.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xu stood more than seven chi tall, light and nimble, skilled at horsemanship and archery, with several scales like dragon scales under both armpits.

sentences.zh: 既負其雄武，又每從北征，在成祖左右，時媒孽東宮事，譖解縉至死，黃淮等皆系獄。

translations.literal: Trusting in his martial prowess and accompanying every northern campaign at the Yongle Emperor's side, he constantly slandered the eastern palace; he falsely accused Xie Jin to death, and Huang Huai and others were all imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Trusting in his martial prowess, he accompanied every northern campaign at the Yongle Emperor's side and constantly slandered the crown prince. He falsely accused Xie Jin to death, and Huang Huai and others were all imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 十三年五月改封青州，又不欲行。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the thirteenth year he was transferred to Qingzhou, and again he did not wish to go.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the thirteenth year he was transferred to Qingzhou, and again he did not wish to go.

sentences.zh: 成祖始疑之，賜敕曰：「既受藩封，豈可常居京邸！

translations.literal: The Yongle Emperor began to suspect him and sent an edict: "Having received a princely fief, how can you always dwell in the capital residence!
translations.idiomatic: The Yongle Emperor began to suspect him and sent an edict: "Having received a princely fief, how can you always dwell in the capital residence!

sentences.zh: 前以雲南遠憚行，今封青州，又托故欲留侍，前後殆非實意，茲命更不可辭。」

translations.literal: Before you feared the distance to Yunnan and would not go; now enfeoffed at Qingzhou, you again invent pretexts to remain in attendance—your intent from first to last is hardly sincere. This order you must not refuse."
translations.idiomatic: Before you feared the distance to Yunnan and would not go. Now, enfeoffed at Qingzhou, you again invent pretexts to remain in attendance—your intent from first to last is hardly sincere. This order you must not refuse."

sentences.zh: 然高煦遷延自如。

translations.literal: Yet Gao Xu delayed as before.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Gao Xu delayed as before.

sentences.zh: 私選各衛健士，又募兵三千人，不隸籍兵部，縱使劫掠。

translations.literal: He privately selected stalwart soldiers from the various guards, also recruited three thousand troops not registered with the Ministry of War, and let them plunder.
translations.idiomatic: He privately selected stalwart soldiers from the various guards, recruited three thousand troops not registered with the Ministry of War, and let them plunder at will.

sentences.zh: 兵馬指揮徐野驢擒治之。

translations.literal: The cavalry commander Xu Yelü captured and punished them.
translations.idiomatic: The cavalry commander Xu Yelü captured and punished them.

sentences.zh: 高煦怒，手鐵瓜撾殺野驢，眾莫敢言。

translations.literal: Gao Xu was angered, and with his iron mace in hand beat Xu Yelü to death; none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xu was enraged. With his iron mace in hand he beat Xu Yelü to death, and none dared speak out.

sentences.zh: 遂僭用乘輿器物。

translations.literal: He then usurped imperial carriage and regalia.
translations.idiomatic: He then usurped the regalia of the imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 成祖聞之怒。

translations.literal: When the Yongle Emperor heard of it he was angered.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yongle Emperor heard of it he was enraged.

sentences.zh: 十四年十月還南京，盡得其不法數十事，切責之，褫冠服，囚系西華門內，將廢為庶人。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the fourteenth year he returned to Nanjing, fully ascertained dozens of his unlawful acts, sternly rebuked him, stripped his cap and robes, imprisoned him inside the Xihua Gate, and was about to reduce him to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the fourteenth year he returned to Nanjing, ascertained dozens of Gao Xu's unlawful acts, sternly rebuked him, stripped his cap and robes, imprisoned him inside the Xihua Gate, and was about to reduce him to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 仁宗涕泣力救，乃削兩護衛，誅其左右狎匿諸人。

translations.literal: The Renzong wept and pleaded hard to save him; thereupon two bodyguards were stripped away and his intimate attendants were executed.
translations.idiomatic: The Renzong wept and pleaded hard to save him. Thereupon two bodyguards were stripped away and his intimate attendants were executed.

sentences.zh: 明年三月徙封樂安州，趣即日行。

translations.literal: In the third month of the following year he was transferred to Le'an Prefecture and ordered to depart that very day.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the following year he was transferred to Le'an Prefecture and ordered to depart that very day.

sentences.zh: 高煦至樂安，怨望，異謀益急。

translations.literal: When Gao Xu reached Le'an he was resentful and discontent; his treasonous plotting grew ever more urgent.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Xu reached Le'an he was filled with resentment and discontent, and his treasonous plotting grew ever more urgent.

sentences.zh: 仁宗數以書戒，不悛。

translations.literal: The Renzong repeatedly sent letters of warning; he did not reform.
translations.idiomatic: The Renzong repeatedly sent letters of warning, but he did not reform.

sentences.zh: 成祖北征晏駕。

translations.literal: The Yongle Emperor died on a northern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongle Emperor died while on a northern campaign.

sentences.zh: 高煦子瞻圻在北京，覘朝廷事馳報，一晝夜六七行。

translations.literal: Gao Xu's son Zhan Qi was in Beijing, spying on court affairs and galloping back with reports six or seven times in a day and night.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xu's son Zhan Qi was in Beijing, spying on court affairs and galloping back with reports six or seven times in a day and night.

sentences.zh: 高煦亦日遣人潛伺京師，幸有變。

translations.literal: Gao Xu also daily sent men to secretly watch the capital, hoping for upheaval.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xu also sent men daily to secretly watch the capital, hoping for upheaval.

sentences.zh: 仁宗知之，顧益厚遇。

translations.literal: The Renzong knew of it but treated him all the more generously.
translations.idiomatic: The Renzong knew of it but treated him all the more generously.

sentences.zh: 遺書召至，增歲祿，賜賚萬計，仍命歸藩。

translations.literal: By testamentary letter he summoned him, increased his annual stipend, bestowed gifts numbering in the tens of thousands, and still ordered him to return to his fief.
translations.idiomatic: By testamentary letter he summoned Gao Xu, increased his annual stipend, bestowed gifts numbering in the tens of thousands, and still ordered him to return to his fief.

sentences.zh: 封其長子為世子，余皆郡王。

translations.literal: His eldest son was enfeoffed as heir apparent; the rest were all made commandery princes.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son was enfeoffed as heir apparent; the rest were all made commandery princes.

sentences.zh: 先是，瞻圻怨父殺其母，屢發父過惡。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhan Qi resented his father for killing his mother and repeatedly exposed his father's faults and crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Zhan Qi resented his father for killing his mother and repeatedly exposed his father's faults and crimes.

sentences.zh: 成祖曰：「爾父子何忍也！」

translations.literal: The Yongle Emperor said: "How can you father and son be so cruel to each other!"
translations.idiomatic: The Yongle Emperor said, "How can you father and son be so cruel to each other!"

sentences.zh: 至是高煦入朝，悉上瞻圻前後覘報中朝事。

translations.literal: Thereupon Gao Xu came to court and fully submitted Zhan Qi's earlier and later spying reports on the central court.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Gao Xu came to court and fully submitted Zhan Qi's earlier and later intelligence reports on the central court.

sentences.zh: 仁宗召示瞻圻曰：「汝處父子兄弟間，讒構至此，稚子不足誅。」

translations.literal: The Renzong summoned Zhan Qi and showed him, saying: "You stand between father and brothers and have slandered to this extent; a young child is not worth executing."
translations.idiomatic: The Renzong summoned Zhan Qi and said to him, "Caught between father and brothers, you have slandered to this extent. A young child is not worth executing."

sentences.zh: 遣守鳳陽皇陵。

translations.literal: He was sent to guard the imperial mausoleum at Fengyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent to guard the imperial mausoleum at Fengyang.

sentences.zh: 未幾，仁宗崩，宣宗自南京奔喪。高煦謀伏兵邀於路，倉卒不果。及帝即位，賜高煦及趙王視他府特厚。高煦日有請，並陳利國安民四事。帝命有司施行，仍復書謝之。因語群臣曰：「皇祖嘗諭皇考，謂叔有異志，宜備之。然皇考待之極厚。如今所言，果出於誠，則是舊心已革，可不順從。」凡有求請，皆曲徇其意。高煦益自肆。

translations.literal: Before long, Renzong died, and Xuanzong hurried from Nanjing to mourning. Gaoxu plotted to set an ambush and intercept him on the road, but in the rush he did not succeed. When the emperor came to the throne, his gifts to Gaoxu and the Prince of Zhao were especially generous compared with the other princely establishments. Gaoxu made requests every day and also presented four measures to benefit the state and settle the people. The emperor ordered the responsible offices to put them into effect and wrote back to thank him. He then said to the assembled ministers, "The imperial ancestor once instructed my imperial father, saying that my uncle had different ambitions and should be guarded against. Yet my imperial father treated him with extreme generosity. If what he says now truly comes from sincerity, then his former mind has already changed; how can I not comply?" In all his requests, the emperor bent to follow his wishes. Gaoxu became increasingly unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: Not long afterward Renzong died, and Xuanzong hastened from Nanjing to attend the mourning. Gaoxu planned to place troops in ambush and intercept him on the road, but the moment was too hurried and the plot failed. After Xuanzong took the throne, his gifts to Gaoxu and to the Prince of Zhao were especially generous compared with other princely households. Gaoxu made requests daily and also submitted four proposals for strengthening the state and pacifying the people. The emperor ordered the offices to implement them and wrote back to thank him. He then told the ministers, "The imperial ancestor once warned my imperial father that my uncle had rebellious ambitions and should be guarded against. Yet my imperial father treated him with the greatest generosity. If what he says now truly comes from sincerity, then his old intentions have changed; how could I refuse him?" Whatever Gaoxu requested, the emperor bent over backward to comply. Gaoxu grew still more willful.

sentences.zh: 宣德元年八月，遂反。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Xuande he rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the first year of the Xuande reign he rebelled.

sentences.zh: 遣其親信枚青等潛至京師，約舊功臣為內應。

translations.literal: He sent his trusted followers Mei Qing and others secretly to the capital to arrange with former meritorious officials for internal support.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his trusted followers Mei Qing and others secretly to the capital to arrange with former meritorious officials for internal support.

sentences.zh: 英國公張輔執之以聞。

translations.literal: The Duke of Ying, Zhang Fu, arrested them and reported it.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Ying, Zhang Fu, arrested them and reported it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 時高煦已約山東都指揮靳榮等，又散弓刀旂幟於衛所，盡奪傍郡縣畜馬。

translations.literal: By then Gao Xu had already arranged with the Shandong regional commander Jin Rong and others, also distributed bows, blades, banners, and flags to the guard posts, and seized all horses held by neighboring prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: By then Gao Xu had already arranged with the Shandong regional commander Jin Rong and others, distributed bows, blades, banners, and flags to the guard posts, and seized all horses held by neighboring prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 立五軍：指揮王斌領前軍，韋達左軍，千戶盛堅右軍，知州朱恒後軍，諸子各監一軍，高煦自將中軍。

translations.literal: He established five armies: the commander Wang Bin led the vanguard, Wei Da the left army, the chiliarch Sheng Jian the right army, the prefect Zhu Heng the rear army; each of his sons supervised one army, and Gao Xu personally commanded the center army.
translations.idiomatic: He established five armies: the commander Wang Bin led the vanguard, Wei Da the left army, the chiliarch Sheng Jian the right army, the prefect Zhu Heng the rear army; each of his sons supervised one army, and Gao Xu personally commanded the center army.

sentences.zh: 世子瞻坦居守，指揮韋弘、韋興，千戶王玉、李智領四哨。

translations.literal: The heir apparent Zhan Tan remained to hold the city; the commanders Wei Hong and Wei Xing and the chiliarchs Wang Yu and Li Zhi led four outposts.
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent Zhan Tan remained to hold the city; the commanders Wei Hong and Wei Xing and the chiliarchs Wang Yu and Li Zhi led four outposts.

sentences.zh: 部署已定，偽授王斌、朱恒等太師、都督、尚書等官。

translations.literal: Once the deployment was set, he falsely appointed Wang Bin, Zhu Heng, and others as grand preceptor, regional commander, minister, and other offices.
translations.idiomatic: Once the deployment was set, he falsely appointed Wang Bin, Zhu Heng, and others as grand preceptor, regional commander, minister, and other offices.

sentences.zh: 御史李濬以父喪家居，高煦招之，不從，變姓名，間道詣京師上變。

translations.literal: The censor Li Jun was at home in mourning for his father; Gao Xu recruited him but he refused, changed his name, took a byway to the capital, and reported the rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The censor Li Jun was at home in mourning for his father. Gao Xu recruited him but he refused, changed his name, took a byway to the capital, and reported the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 帝猶不忍加兵，遣中官侯泰賜高煦書。

translations.literal: The emperor still could not bear to send troops and dispatched the eunuch Hou Tai to deliver a letter to Gao Xu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still could not bear to send troops and dispatched the eunuch Hou Tai to deliver a letter to Gao Xu.

sentences.zh: 泰至，高煦盛兵見泰，南面坐，大言曰：「永樂中信讒，削我護衛，徙我樂安。

translations.literal: When Tai arrived, Gao Xu displayed his troops to receive him, sat facing south, and spoke loudly: "In the Yongle reign slanderous reports stripped my bodyguards and moved me to Le'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Tai arrived, Gao Xu displayed his troops to receive him, sat facing south, and spoke loudly, "In the Yongle reign slanderous reports stripped my bodyguards and moved me to Le'an.

sentences.zh: 仁宗徒以金帛餌我，我豈能郁郁居此！

translations.literal: The Renzong merely baited me with gold and silk—how could I dwell here in gloom!
translations.idiomatic: The Renzong merely baited me with gold and silk—how could I dwell here in gloom!

sentences.zh: 汝歸報，急縛奸臣夏原吉等來，徐議我所欲。」

translations.literal: Go back and report: bind the traitorous ministers Xia Yuanji and the rest at once and bring them here, then we may slowly discuss what I want."
translations.idiomatic: Go back and report: bind the traitorous ministers Xia Yuanji and the rest at once and bring them here, then we may slowly discuss what I want."

sentences.zh: 泰懼，唯唯而已。

translations.literal: Tai was afraid and could only murmur assent.
translations.idiomatic: Tai was afraid and could only murmur assent.

sentences.zh: 比還，帝問漢王何言，治兵何如，泰皆不敢以實對。

translations.literal: When he returned the emperor asked what the Prince of Han had said and how his troops were arrayed; Tai dared not answer truthfully on any point.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned the emperor asked what the Prince of Han had said and how his troops were arrayed; Tai dared not answer truthfully on any point.

sentences.zh: 是月，高煦遣百戶陳剛進疏，更為書與公侯大臣，多所指斥。

translations.literal: That month Gao Xu sent the centurion Chen Gang to submit a memorial and also wrote letters to the dukes and grand ministers, full of accusations.
translations.idiomatic: That month Gao Xu sent the centurion Chen Gang to submit a memorial and also wrote letters to the dukes and grand ministers, full of accusations.

sentences.zh: 帝嘆曰：「漢王果反。」

translations.literal: The emperor sighed and said: "The Prince of Han has indeed rebelled."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed and said, "The Prince of Han has indeed rebelled."

sentences.zh: 乃議遣陽武侯薛祿將兵往討。

translations.literal: Thereupon it was proposed to send the Marquis of Yangwu, Xue Lu, to lead troops to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon it was proposed to send the Marquis of Yangwu, Xue Lu, to lead troops to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 大學士楊榮等勸帝親征。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Yang Rong and others urged the emperor to campaign in person.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Yang Rong and others urged the emperor to campaign in person.

sentences.zh: 帝是之。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 張輔奏曰：「高煦素懦，願假臣兵二萬，擒獻闕下。」

translations.literal: Zhang Fu memorialized: "Gao Xu has always been timid; grant me twenty thousand troops and I will capture him and present him at court."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fu memorialized, "Gao Xu has always been timid; grant me twenty thousand troops and I will capture him and present him at court."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿誠足擒賊，顧朕初即位，小人或懷二心，不親行，不足安反側。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "You could indeed capture the rebel, but I have just taken the throne and petty men may harbor divided loyalties; unless I go in person I cannot reassure the wavering."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You could indeed capture the rebel, but I have just taken the throne and petty men may harbor divided loyalties; unless I go in person I cannot reassure the wavering."

sentences.zh: 於是車駕發京師，過楊村，馬上顧從臣曰：「度高煦計安出？」

translations.literal: Thereupon the imperial carriage set out from the capital; passing Yangcun, the emperor turned on his horse to his followers and said: "What plan do you think Gao Xu will adopt?"
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the imperial carriage set out from the capital. Passing Yangcun, the emperor turned on his horse to his followers and said, "What plan do you think Gao Xu will adopt?"

sentences.zh: 或對曰：「必先取濟南為巢窟。」

translations.literal: Someone answered: "He will surely seize Jinan first as his lair."
translations.idiomatic: Someone answered, "He will surely seize Jinan first as his lair."

sentences.zh: 或對曰：「彼曩不肯離南京，今必引兵南下。」

translations.literal: Someone answered: "He would not leave Nanjing before; now he will surely lead his army south."
translations.idiomatic: Someone answered, "He would not leave Nanjing before; now he will surely lead his army south."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「不然。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Not so.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Not so.

sentences.zh: 濟南雖近，未易攻，聞大軍至，亦不暇攻。

translations.literal: Jinan is close but not easy to attack; hearing the great army has arrived, he will not have leisure to attack it.
translations.idiomatic: Jinan is close but not easy to attack; hearing the great army has arrived, he will not have leisure to attack it.

sentences.zh: 護衛軍家樂安，必內顧，不肯徑趨南京。

translations.literal: The bodyguard soldiers' families are at Le'an; they will surely look homeward and will not rush straight for Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: The bodyguard soldiers' families are at Le'an; they will surely look homeward and will not rush straight for Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 高煦外誇詐，內實怯，臨事狐疑不能斷。

translations.literal: Gao Xu outwardly boasts and deceives but inwardly is truly timid; facing events he is hesitant and cannot decide.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xu outwardly boasts and deceives but inwardly is truly timid; facing events he is hesitant and cannot decide.

sentences.zh: 今敢反者，輕朕年少新立，眾心未附，不能親征耳。

translations.literal: He dares rebel now because he thinks me young and newly enthroned, with hearts not yet attached, and unable to campaign in person.
translations.idiomatic: He dares rebel now because he thinks me young and newly enthroned, with hearts not yet attached, and unable to campaign in person.

sentences.zh: 今聞朕行，已膽落，敢出戰乎？

translations.literal: Now that he hears I am coming, his courage has already failed—will he dare give battle?
translations.idiomatic: Now that he hears I am coming, his courage has already failed—will he dare give battle?

sentences.zh: 至即擒矣。」

translations.literal: When we arrive he will be captured at once."
translations.idiomatic: When we arrive he will be captured at once."

sentences.zh: 高煦初聞祿等將兵，攘臂大喜，以為易與。

translations.literal: When Gao Xu first heard that Xue Lu and others were leading troops he rubbed his arms in delight, thinking them easy opponents.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Xu first heard that Xue Lu and others were leading troops he rubbed his arms in delight, thinking them easy opponents.

sentences.zh: 及聞親征，始懼。

translations.literal: When he heard of the personal campaign he began to fear.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard of the personal campaign he began to fear.

sentences.zh: 時有從樂安來歸者，帝厚賞之，令還諭其眾。

translations.literal: At the time some who had come over from Le'an were richly rewarded; the emperor ordered them to return and instruct the rest.
translations.idiomatic: At the time some who had come over from Le'an were richly rewarded; the emperor ordered them to return and instruct the rest.

sentences.zh: 仍遺書高煦曰：「張敖失國，始於貫高；

translations.literal: He still sent a letter to Gao Xu saying: "Zhang Ao lost his state, beginning with Guan Gao;
translations.idiomatic: He still sent a letter to Gao Xu saying, "Zhang Ao lost his state, beginning with Guan Gao;

sentences.zh: 淮南被誅，成於伍被。

translations.literal: The Prince of Huainan was executed, accomplished by Wu Bei.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Huainan was executed, accomplished by Wu Bei.

sentences.zh: 今六師壓境，王即出倡謀者，朕與王除過，恩禮如初。

translations.literal: Now the six armies press the border; if the prince at once hands over the chief plotters, I will wipe the slate clean with the prince and treat him with grace as before.
