translations.idiomatic: Now the six armies press the border; if the prince at once hands over the chief plotters, I will wipe the slate clean with the prince and treat him with grace as before.

sentences.zh: 不然，一戰成擒，或以王為奇貨，縛以來獻，悔無及矣。」

translations.literal: Otherwise, one battle and you are captured—or someone may treat the prince as a rare prize, bind you and present you as tribute, and then regret will be too late."
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, one battle and you are captured—or someone may treat the prince as a rare prize, bind you and present you as tribute, and then regret will be too late."

sentences.zh: 前鋒至樂安，高煦約詰旦出戰。

translations.literal: The vanguard reached Le'an; Gao Xu arranged to give battle at dawn.
translations.idiomatic: The vanguard reached Le'an; Gao Xu arranged to give battle at dawn.

sentences.zh: 帝令大軍蓐食兼行，駐蹕樂安城北，壁其四門。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the great army to eat at dawn and march together, halting north of Le'an city and walling its four gates.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the great army to eat at dawn and march together, halting north of Le'an city and walling its four gates.

sentences.zh: 賊乘城守，王師發神機銃箭，聲震如雷。

translations.literal: The rebels manned the walls in defense; the imperial army fired divine engine bolts and arrows, the sound thundering like rolling thunder.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels manned the walls in defense; the imperial army fired divine engine bolts and arrows, the sound thundering like rolling thunder.

sentences.zh: 諸將請即攻城。

translations.literal: The generals asked to assault the city at once.
translations.idiomatic: The generals asked to assault the city at once.

sentences.zh: 帝不許。

translations.literal: The emperor would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not permit it.

sentences.zh: 再敕諭高煦，皆不答。

translations.literal: Again he sent edicts instructing Gao Xu; there was no answer.
translations.idiomatic: Again he sent edicts instructing Gao Xu; there was no answer.

sentences.zh: 城中人多欲執獻高煦者，高煦大懼。

translations.literal: Many in the city wished to seize and present Gao Xu; Gao Xu was greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Many in the city wished to seize and present Gao Xu; Gao Xu was greatly afraid.

sentences.zh: 乃密遣人詣行幄，願假今夕訣妻子，即出歸罪。

translations.literal: He secretly sent a man to the imperial camp, asking leave to bid farewell to wife and children this night and then come out to submit.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly sent a man to the imperial camp, asking leave to bid farewell to wife and children this night and then come out to submit.

sentences.zh: 帝許之。

translations.literal: The emperor granted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted it.

sentences.zh: 是夜，高煦盡焚兵器及通逆謀書。

translations.literal: That night Gao Xu burned all weapons and treasonous correspondence.
translations.idiomatic: That night Gao Xu burned all weapons and treasonous correspondence.

sentences.zh: 明日，帝移蹕樂安城南。

translations.literal: The next day the emperor moved his camp to the south of Le'an.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the emperor moved his camp to the south of Le'an.

sentences.zh: 高煦將出城，王斌等力止曰：「寧一戰死，無為人擒。」

translations.literal: When Gao Xu was about to leave the city, Wang Bin and others forcefully stopped him, saying: "Better die in one battle than be captured by others."
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Xu was about to leave the city, Wang Bin and others forcefully stopped him, saying, "Better die in one battle than be captured by others."

sentences.zh: 高煦紿斌等復入宮，遂潛從間道出見帝。

translations.literal: Gao Xu deceived Bin and the others into re-entering the palace, then secretly slipped out by a hidden path to appear before the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xu deceived Bin and the others into re-entering the palace, then secretly slipped out by a hidden path to appear before the emperor.

sentences.zh: 群臣請正典刑。

translations.literal: The ministers asked that proper punishment be applied.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers asked that proper punishment be applied.

sentences.zh: 不允。

translations.literal: It was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: It was not granted.

sentences.zh: 以劾章示之，高煦頓首言：「臣罪萬萬死，惟陛下命。」

translations.literal: The impeachment memorial was shown to him; Gao Xu kowtowed and said: "Your subject's crime deserves ten thousand deaths; I await Your Majesty's command."
translations.idiomatic: The impeachment memorial was shown to him; Gao Xu kowtowed and said, "Your subject's crime deserves ten thousand deaths; I await Your Majesty's command."

sentences.zh: 帝令高煦為書召諸子，余黨悉就擒。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Gao Xu to write letters summoning his sons; the remaining conspirators were all captured.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Gao Xu to write letters summoning his sons; the remaining conspirators were all captured.

sentences.zh: 赦城中罪，脅從者不問。

translations.literal: Crimes in the city were pardoned; those coerced to follow were not questioned.
translations.idiomatic: Crimes in the city were pardoned; those coerced to follow were not questioned.

sentences.zh: 命薛祿及尚書張本鎮撫樂安，改曰武定州，遂班師。

translations.literal: Xue Lu and Minister Zhang Ben were ordered to pacify Le'an; it was renamed Wuding Prefecture, and the army withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Lu and Minister Zhang Ben were ordered to pacify Le'an; it was renamed Wuding Prefecture, and the army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 廢高煦父子為庶人，築室西安門內錮之。

translations.literal: Gao Xu and his sons were reduced to commoner status and walled up in dwellings inside the Xi'an Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xu and his sons were reduced to commoner status and walled up in dwellings inside the Xi'an Gate.

sentences.zh: 王斌等皆伏誅，惟長史李默以嘗諫免死，謫口北為民。

translations.literal: Wang Bin and the rest were all executed; only the chief administrator Li Mo was spared death for having once remonstrated and was banished to the northern frontier as a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bin and the rest were all executed; only the chief administrator Li Mo was spared death for having once remonstrated and was banished to the northern frontier as a commoner.

sentences.zh: 天津、青州、滄州、山西諸都督指揮約舉城應者，事覺相繼誅，凡六百四十余人，其故縱與藏匿坐死戍邊者一千五百余人，編邊氓者七百二十人。

translations.literal: Regional commanders and commanders at Tianjin, Qingzhou, Cangzhou, and Shanxi who had agreed to rise when the cities were taken were exposed and executed in succession, six hundred forty-odd in all; those who had knowingly abetted or concealed them and were sentenced to death or frontier service numbered more than fifteen hundred, and seven hundred twenty border commoners were enrolled for service.
translations.idiomatic: Regional commanders and commanders at Tianjin, Qingzhou, Cangzhou, and Shanxi who had agreed to rise when the cities were taken were exposed and executed in succession, six hundred forty-odd in all; those who had knowingly abetted or concealed them and were sentenced to death or frontier service numbered more than fifteen hundred, and seven hundred twenty border commoners were enrolled for service.

sentences.zh: 帝制《東征記》以示群臣。

translations.literal: The emperor composed the Record of the Eastern Campaign and showed it to the ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor composed the Record of the Eastern Campaign and showed it to the ministers.

sentences.zh: 高煦及諸子相繼皆死。

translations.literal: Gao Xu and his sons died one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xu and his sons died one after another.

sentences.zh: 趙簡王高燧，成祖第三子。

translations.literal: Prince Jian of Zhao, Gao Sui, was the Yongle Emperor's third son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jian of Zhao, Gao Sui, was the Yongle Emperor's third son.

sentences.zh: 永樂二年封。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed in the second year of Yongle.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed in the second year of the Yongle reign.

sentences.zh: 尋命居北京，詔有司，政務皆啟王後行。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to reside in Beijing; an edict to the officials declared that all government affairs were to be reported to the prince before action.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was ordered to reside in Beijing; an edict to the officials declared that all government affairs were to be reported to the prince before action.

sentences.zh: 歲時朝京師，辭歸，太子輒送之江東驛。

translations.literal: At the seasonal visits to the capital, when he took leave to return the crown prince always saw him off at the Jiangdong post station.
translations.idiomatic: At the seasonal visits to the capital, when he took leave to return the crown prince always saw him off at the Jiangdong post station.

sentences.zh: 高燧恃寵，多行不法，又與漢王高煦謀奪嫡，時時譖太子。

translations.literal: Gao Sui relied on favor, committed many unlawful acts, and also plotted with the Prince of Han, Gao Xu, to seize the succession, constantly slandering the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Sui relied on favor, committed many unlawful acts, and also plotted with the Prince of Han, Gao Xu, to seize the succession, constantly slandering the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 於是太子宮寮多得罪。

translations.literal: Thereupon many in the crown prince's household staff fell into disgrace.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon many in the crown prince's household staff fell into disgrace.

sentences.zh: 七年，帝聞其不法事，大怒，誅其長史顧晟，褫高燧冠服，以太子力解，得免。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the emperor heard of his unlawful acts, was greatly angered, executed his chief administrator Gu Sheng, stripped Gao Sui of cap and robes, and through the crown prince's strenuous intercession he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year the emperor heard of his unlawful acts, was greatly angered, executed his chief administrator Gu Sheng, stripped Gao Sui of cap and robes, and through the crown prince's strenuous intercession he was spared.

sentences.zh: 擇國子司業趙亨道、董子莊為長史輔導之，高燧稍改行。

translations.literal: The National University vice chancellors Zhao Hengdao and Dong Zizhuang were chosen as chief administrators to guide him, and Gao Sui gradually reformed his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: The National University vice chancellors Zhao Hengdao and Dong Zizhuang were chosen as chief administrators to guide him, and Gao Sui gradually reformed his conduct.

sentences.zh: 二十一年五月，帝不豫。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the twenty-first year the emperor fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the twenty-first year the emperor fell ill.

sentences.zh: 護衛指揮孟賢等結欽天監官王射成及內侍楊慶養子造偽詔，謀進毒於帝，俟晏駕，詔從中下，廢太子，立趙王。

translations.literal: The bodyguard commander Meng Xian and others joined with the Directorate of Astronomy official Wang Shecheng and the eunuch Yang Qing's adopted son to forge an edict, plotting to administer poison to the emperor; when he died they would issue the edict from within, depose the crown prince, and establish the Prince of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: The bodyguard commander Meng Xian and others joined with the Directorate of Astronomy official Wang Shecheng and the eunuch Yang Qing's adopted son to forge an edict, plotting to administer poison to the emperor; when he died they would issue the edict from within, depose the crown prince, and establish the Prince of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 總旗王瑜姻家高以正者，為賢等畫謀，謀定告瑜。

translations.literal: Gao Yizheng, a relative by marriage of the company commander Wang Yu, drew up the plot for Xian and the others; once the plot was set he informed Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yizheng, a relative by marriage of the company commander Wang Yu, drew up the plot for Xian and the others; once the plot was set he informed Yu.

sentences.zh: 瑜上變。

translations.literal: Yu reported the treason.
translations.idiomatic: Yu reported the treason.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「豈應有此！」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "How could such a thing be!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "How could such a thing be!"

sentences.zh: 立捕賢，得為偽詔。

translations.literal: He immediately arrested Xian and obtained the forged edict.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately arrested Xian and obtained the forged edict.

sentences.zh: 賢等皆伏誅，陛瑜遼海衛千戶。

translations.literal: Xian and the rest were all executed; Yu was promoted to chiliarch of the Liaohai Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Xian and the rest were all executed; Yu was promoted to chiliarch of the Liaohai Guard.

sentences.zh: 帝顧高燧曰：「爾為之耶？」

translations.literal: The emperor turned to Gao Sui and said: "Did you do this?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned to Gao Sui and said, "Did you do this?"

sentences.zh: 高燧大懼，不能言。

translations.literal: Gao Sui was greatly afraid and could not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Sui was greatly afraid and could not speak.

sentences.zh: 太子力為之解曰：「此下人所為，高燧必不與知。」

translations.literal: The crown prince strenuously interceded for him, saying: "This was the work of petty men; Gao Sui surely knew nothing of it."
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince strenuously interceded for him, saying, "This was the work of petty men; Gao Sui surely knew nothing of it."

sentences.zh: 自是益斂戢。

translations.literal: From then on he restrained himself all the more.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he restrained himself all the more.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，加漢、趙二王歲祿二萬石。明年，之國彰德，辭常山左右二護衛。宣宗即位，賜田園八十頃。帝擒高煦歸，至單橋，尚書陳山迎駕，言曰：「趙王與高煦共謀逆久矣，宜移兵彰德，擒趙王。否則趙王反側不自安，異日復勞聖慮。」帝未決。時惟楊士奇以為不可。山復邀尚書蹇義、夏原吉共請。帝曰：「先帝友愛二叔甚。漢王自絕於天，朕不敢赦。趙王反形未著，朕不忍負先帝也。」及高煦至京，亦言嘗遣人與趙通謀。戶部主事李儀請削其護衛，尚書張本亦以為言。帝不聽。既而言者益眾。明年，帝以其詞及群臣章遣駙馬都尉廣平侯袁容持示高燧。高燧大懼，乃請還常山中護衛及群牧所、儀衛司官校。帝命收其所還護衛，而與儀衛司。宣德六年薨。

translations.literal: When Renzong came to the throne, he added twenty thousand shi to the annual stipends of the princes of Han and Zhao. The next year, Gao Sui went to his state at Zhangde and declined the left and right guards of Changshan. When Xuanzong came to the throne, he bestowed eighty qing of fields and gardens on him. After the emperor captured Gaoxu and returned, when he reached Shanqiao, Minister Chen Shan came to welcome the imperial carriage and said, "The Prince of Zhao has been plotting rebellion with Gaoxu for a long time. Troops should be moved to Zhangde to seize the Prince of Zhao. Otherwise the Prince of Zhao will be uneasy in his uncertainty, and on another day he will again trouble Your Majesty's thoughts." The emperor had not decided. At the time only Yang Shiqi considered it impermissible. Shan again invited Ministers Jian Yi and Xia Yuanji to request it together. The emperor said, "The late emperor loved his two younger brothers very much. The Prince of Han cut himself off from Heaven, and I do not dare pardon him. The Prince of Zhao's rebellious form has not yet become manifest, and I cannot bear to betray the late emperor." When Gaoxu reached the capital, he also said that he had once sent men to communicate plots with Zhao. Li Yi, supervising secretary in the Ministry of Revenue, requested that Zhao's guards be cut down, and Minister Zhang Ben also spoke of it. The emperor did not listen. After this, those who spoke of it became more numerous. The next year, the emperor took those statements and the ministers' memorials and sent Imperial Son-in-law Commandant Yuan Rong, Marquis of Guangping, to carry them and show them to Gao Sui. Gao Sui was greatly afraid and requested to return the central guard of Changshan, the herd offices, and the officers and soldiers of the Office of Ceremonial Guards. The emperor ordered the guards he returned to be taken back but left him the Office of Ceremonial Guards. He died in Xuande year six.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong came to the throne, he increased the annual stipends of the princes of Han and Zhao by twenty thousand shi. The following year Gao Sui went to his state at Zhangde and declined the left and right guards of Changshan. When Xuanzong came to the throne, he granted him eighty qing of fields and gardens. After the emperor captured Gaoxu and was returning, he reached Shanqiao, where Minister Chen Shan came out to meet the imperial carriage and said, "The Prince of Zhao has long plotted rebellion with Gaoxu. Troops should be moved to Zhangde and the Prince of Zhao seized. Otherwise the Prince of Zhao, restless and insecure, will one day again trouble Your Majesty's mind." The emperor had not yet decided. At the time only Yang Shiqi thought this should not be done. Chen Shan then invited Ministers Jian Yi and Xia Yuanji to join the request. The emperor said, "The late emperor dearly loved his two younger brothers. The Prince of Han cut himself off from Heaven, so I dare not pardon him. But the Prince of Zhao's rebellion has not taken visible form, and I cannot bear to betray the late emperor." When Gaoxu reached the capital, he too said that he had sent men to plot with Zhao. Li Yi, a supervising secretary in the Ministry of Revenue, requested that Zhao's guards be reduced, and Minister Zhang Ben said the same. The emperor would not listen. Afterward, more and more men spoke of it. The next year, the emperor sent Imperial Son-in-law Commandant Yuan Rong, Marquis of Guangping, to show Gao Sui those statements and the ministers' memorials. Terrified, Gao Sui asked to return the central guard of Changshan, the herd offices, and the officers and men of the Office of Ceremonial Guards. The emperor ordered the returned guard taken back but left him the Office of Ceremonial Guards. Gao Sui died in Xuande 6.

sentences.zh: 子惠王蟾塙嗣，景泰五年薨。

translations.literal: His son the Prince of Hui, Chan Huang, succeeded and died in the fifth year of Jingtai.
translations.idiomatic: His son the Prince of Hui, Chan Huang, succeeded and died in the fifth year of the Jingtai reign.

sentences.zh: 子悼王祈钅茲嗣，天順四年薨。

translations.literal: His son the Prince of Dao, Qi Ci, succeeded and died in the fourth year of Tianshun.
translations.idiomatic: His son the Prince of Dao, Qi Ci, succeeded and died in the fourth year of the Tianshun reign.

sentences.zh: 子靖王見灂嗣。

translations.literal: His son the Prince of Jing, Jian Zhuo, succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son the Prince of Jing, Jian Zhuo, succeeded.

sentences.zh: 惠王、悼王皆頗有過失，至見灂惡尤甚，屢賊殺人，又嘗乘醉欲殺其叔父。

translations.literal: The Princes of Hui and Dao both had considerable faults; as for Jian Zhuo his wickedness was especially severe—he repeatedly murdered as a bandit and once, drunk, tried to kill his uncle.
translations.idiomatic: The Princes of Hui and Dao both had considerable faults; as for Jian Zhuo his wickedness was especially severe—he repeatedly murdered as a bandit and once, drunk, tried to kill his uncle.

sentences.zh: 成化十二年，事聞，詔奪祿米三之二，去冠服，戴民巾，讀書習禮。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Chenghua the matter was reported; an edict stripped two-thirds of his stipend grain, removed his princely cap and robes, made him wear a commoner's headcloth, and ordered him to study the classics and ritual.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of the Chenghua reign the matter was reported; an edict stripped two-thirds of his stipend grain, removed his princely cap and robes, made him wear a commoner's headcloth, and ordered him to study the classics and ritual.

sentences.zh: 其後二年，見灂母妃李氏為之請，得冠服如故。

translations.literal: Two years later Jian Zhuo's mother, Consort Li, petitioned on his behalf and he was restored to his princely cap and robes.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later Jian Zhuo's mother, Consort Li, petitioned on his behalf and he was restored to his princely cap and robes.

sentences.zh: 見灂卒不能改。

translations.literal: Jian Zhuo ultimately could not reform.
translations.idiomatic: Jian Zhuo ultimately could not reform.

sentences.zh: 愛幼子祐枳，遂誣長子祐棌以大逆，復被詔誚讓。

translations.literal: Favoring his younger son You Zhi, he falsely accused his eldest son You Lin of great treason and was again rebuked by imperial edict.
translations.idiomatic: Favoring his younger son You Zhi, he falsely accused his eldest son You Lin of great treason and was again rebuked by imperial edict.

sentences.zh: 弘治十五年薨。

translations.literal: He died in the fifteenth year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifteenth year of the Hongzhi reign.

sentences.zh: 子莊王祐棌嗣，正德十三年薨。

translations.literal: His son the Prince of Zhuang, You Lin, succeeded and died in the thirteenth year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: His son the Prince of Zhuang, You Lin, succeeded and died in the thirteenth year of the Zhengde reign.

sentences.zh: 子康王厚煜嗣，事祖母楊妃以孝聞。

translations.literal: His son the Prince of Kang, Hou Yu, succeeded and was known for filial service to his grandmother, Consort Yang.
translations.idiomatic: His son the Prince of Kang, Hou Yu, succeeded and was known for filial service to his grandmother, Consort Yang.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖七年六月，璽書褒予。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the seventh year of Jiajing an imperial letter praised and rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the seventh year of the Jiajing reign an imperial letter praised and rewarded him.

sentences.zh: 明年冬，境內大饑。

translations.literal: The next winter a great famine struck within his domain.
translations.idiomatic: The next winter a great famine struck within his domain.

sentences.zh: 厚煜上疏，請辭祿一千石以佐振。

translations.literal: Hou Yu submitted a memorial asking to renounce one thousand shi of stipend to aid relief.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Yu submitted a memorial asking to renounce one thousand shi of stipend to aid relief.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉王憂國，詔有司發粟，不允所辭。

translations.literal: The emperor praised the prince's concern for the state, ordered the officials to distribute grain, and did not accept his renunciation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised the prince's concern for the state, ordered the officials to distribute grain, and did not accept his renunciation.

sentences.zh: 及帝南巡，厚煜遠出迎，命益祿三百石。

translations.literal: When the emperor toured the south, Hou Yu went far out to welcome him and was ordered to increase his stipend by three hundred shi.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor toured the south, Hou Yu went far out to welcome him and was ordered to increase his stipend by three hundred shi.

sentences.zh: 厚煜性和厚，構一樓名「思訓」，嘗獨居讀書，文藻贍麗。

translations.literal: Hou Yu's nature was mild and generous; he built a tower called "Reflection on Instruction," often read alone there, and his literary compositions were rich and beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Yu was mild and generous by nature. He built a tower called "Reflection on Instruction," where he often read alone, and his literary compositions were rich and beautiful.

sentences.zh: 宗人輔國將軍祐椋等數犯法，與有司為難。

translations.literal: His clansmen the Supporter-Generals of the State You Liang and others repeatedly broke the law and made trouble for officials.
translations.idiomatic: His clansmen the Supporter-Generals of the State, You Liang and others, repeatedly broke the law and clashed with local officials.

sentences.zh: 厚煜庇祐椋。

translations.literal: Hou Yu sheltered You Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Yu sheltered You Liang.

sentences.zh: 祐椋卒得罪，並見責讓。

translations.literal: You Liang finally offended and both were rebuked.
translations.idiomatic: You Liang finally offended the law, and both men were rebuked.

sentences.zh: 其後有司益務以事裁抑諸宗。

translations.literal: Afterward officials increasingly sought pretexts to restrain the various clansmen.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward officials increasingly seized on pretexts to restrain the various clansmen.

sentences.zh: 洛川王翊鏴奴與通判田時雨之隸爭瓜而毆，時雨捕王奴。

translations.literal: A slave of the Prince of Luochuan, Yi Lin, quarreled over melons with an attendant of the vice-prefect Tian Shiyu and beat him; Shiyu arrested the prince's slave.
translations.idiomatic: A slave of the Prince of Luochuan, Yi Lin, quarreled over melons with an attendant of Vice-prefect Tian Shiyu and beat him; Shiyu arrested the prince's slave.

sentences.zh: 厚煜請解不得，竟論奴充軍。

translations.literal: Hou Yu requested release but could not obtain it; the slave was finally sentenced to military exile.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Yu pleaded for the slave's release in vain; the man was finally sentenced to military exile.

sentences.zh: 未幾，宗室數十人索祿，時雨以宗室毆府官，白於上官。

translations.literal: Before long dozens of clansmen demanded stipends; Shiyu reported that clansmen had beaten prefectural officials to his superiors.
translations.idiomatic: Before long dozens of clansmen demanded their stipends. Shiyu reported that clansmen had beaten prefectural officials to his superiors.

sentences.zh: 知府傅汝礪盡捕各府人。

translations.literal: The prefect Fu Rujie arrested all the men from the various princely residences.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Fu Rujie arrested all the men from the various princely residences.

sentences.zh: 厚煜由是忿恚，竟自縊死。

translations.literal: Hou Yu from this grew resentful and enraged and finally hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Yu grew resentful and enraged over this and finally hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 三十九年十月也。

translations.literal: This was in the tenth month of the thirty-ninth year.
translations.idiomatic: This was in the tenth month of the thirty-ninth year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 厚煜子成臯王載垸疏聞於朝，下法司按問。

translations.literal: Hou Yu's son the Prince of Chenggao, Zai Yuan, memorialized the court; the case was referred to the judicial offices for investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Yu's son the Prince of Chenggao, Zai Yuan, memorialized the court, and the case was referred to the judicial offices for investigation.

sentences.zh: 時雨斬河南市，汝礪戍極邊。

translations.literal: Shiyu was executed in the market at Henan; Rujie was banished to the farthest frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyu was executed in the market at Henan; Rujie was banished to the farthest frontier.

sentences.zh: 厚煜子載培及載培子翊錙皆前卒。

translations.literal: Hou Yu's son Zai Pei and Zai Pei's son Yi Qian had both died earlier.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Yu's son Zai Pei and Zai Pei's son Yi Qian had both died earlier.

sentences.zh: 翊錙子穆王常清嗣，以善行見旌。

translations.literal: Yi Qian's son the Prince of Mu, Chang Qing, succeeded and was honored for good conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Qian's son the Prince of Mu, Chang Qing, succeeded and was honored for good conduct.

sentences.zh: 萬歷四十二年薨。

translations.literal: He died in the forty-second year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the forty-second year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 世子由松前卒，弟壽光王由桂子慈嗣，薨。

translations.literal: The heir apparent You Song died first; his younger brother the Prince of Shouguang's son You Ci succeeded and died.
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent You Song predeceased him; succession passed to the son of his younger brother the Prince of Shouguang, You Ci, who later died.

sentences.zh: 無子，穆王弟常㳛嗣。

translations.literal: Having no son, the Prince of Mu's younger brother Chang Yu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: He had no son, and the Prince of Mu's younger brother Chang Yu succeeded.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十七年，彰德陷，被執。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Chongzhen Zhangde fell and he was captured.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of the Chongzhen reign Zhangde fell and he was taken prisoner.
